items.title: Reinforcement learning, in practice
items.text: This repository collects reinforcement-learning implementations and experiments, from imitation learning and policy gradients to offline RL and language-model training. Use this overview to choose a project, check its current status, and find its instructions.

items.title: Use the right environment
items.text:
Each project manages its own Python dependencies. Python requirements differ between projects.

  • For project work: use the chosen project's directory, README, and pyproject.toml. The offline-to-online project's dependency file is under final_project_offline_online/problem/.
  • For this documentation site: use the repository-root environment. Authored pages live in docs/; documentation authoring explains the tooling and workflow.

items.title: hw1_imitation
items.text:
Train and evaluate action-chunking imitation policies for Push-T.

Training workflow

  1. Prepare episode data, normalization statistics, and action windows with data.
  2. Choose a direct MSE or flow-matching policy in model, then configure and execute a run through train.
  3. Measure validation loss and rollout scores with evaluation. Save or reconstruct self-contained policies through checkpoint.

Supporting modules

  • randomness assigns stable random-stream identities; rng_modules routes generators through layers and manages explicit-RNG dropout.
  • logging_utils formats summaries, writes metric files, and encodes videos. early_stopping tracks evaluation plateaus independently of checkpoint selection.
  • modal_train configures the optional Modal wrapper around the same training driver.

Import functionality from its defining module. This package initializer does not re-export classes or launch training. Checkpoints reconstruct policies and normalization; they do not resume optimizer state or training position.

items.title: checkpoint
items.text:
Save and load self-contained policies for inference or a new training run.

Checkpoint contents

  • Architecture configuration and learned model weights.
  • Runtime training configuration: per-layer dropout probabilities.
  • Observation/action normalization statistics and default flow inference steps.

Use save_policy to write a checkpoint, then load_policy to reconstruct it without the original dataset. Weights are stored on CPU; configuration is plain data.

Loading does not resume a training session. No optimizer, training position, or saved RNG state is restored. Further training uses a new optimizer and caller-owned randomness; saved dropout settings can be explicitly overridden.

items.title: CHECKPOINT_VERSION module-attribute
items.text: CHECKPOINT_VERSION = 1

items.title: save_policy
items.text:
save_policy(path: Path | str, model: BasePolicy, normalizer: Normalizer, *, flow_num_steps: int = 10) -> None

Write the policy, normalization statistics, and inference defaults.

Write sequence

  1. Validate inference steps and normalizer dimensions; assemble CPU weights, copied normalization tensors, and plain configuration data.
  2. Create missing parent directories and serialize to a sibling .tmp file.
  3. Replace the destination after serialization succeeds, then clean up the temporary path.

Calls targeting the same path must not run concurrently because the temporary name is shared. Keep model parameters and statistics stable while saving: CPU weight tensors are detached but not necessarily copied. This helper does not change the model's train/eval mode.

Filesystem and PyTorch serialization errors propagate to the caller. Replacing a file after serialization is not a guarantee of crash-durable storage.

Parameters:

  • path (Path | str) –

    Destination checkpoint file. An existing file is replaced after successful serialization to path with .tmp appended to its suffix.

  • model (BasePolicy) –

    Policy whose architecture, weights, and dropout settings are saved.

  • normalizer (Normalizer) –

    Statistics used for training, with dimensions matching the policy. Export revalidates statistics and copies their numerical storage.

  • flow_num_steps (int, default: 10 ) –

    Positive Python integer default for flow inference. Booleans are rejected. Validated even for MSE policies, which ignore it at sampling.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    Inference steps are invalid, normalizer dimensions do not match, or stored statistics fail validation.

  • OSError –

    A directory, temporary-file, replacement, or cleanup operation fails.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/checkpoint.py 
def save_policy(
    path: Path | str,
    model: BasePolicy,
    normalizer: Normalizer,
    *,
    flow_num_steps: int = 10,
) -> None:
    """Write the policy, normalization statistics, and inference defaults.

    **Write sequence**

    1. Validate inference steps and normalizer dimensions; assemble CPU weights,
       copied normalization tensors, and plain configuration data.
    2. Create missing parent directories and serialize to a sibling `.tmp` file.
    3. Replace the destination after serialization succeeds, then clean up the
       temporary path.

    Calls targeting the same path must not run concurrently because the temporary
    name is shared. Keep model parameters and statistics stable while saving:
    CPU weight tensors are detached but not necessarily copied. This helper does
    not change the model's train/eval mode.

    Filesystem and PyTorch serialization errors propagate to the caller. Replacing
    a file after serialization is not a guarantee of crash-durable storage.

    Args:
        path: Destination checkpoint file. An existing file is replaced after
            successful serialization to `path` with `.tmp` appended to its suffix.
        model: Policy whose architecture, weights, and dropout settings are saved.
        normalizer: Statistics used for training, with dimensions matching the
            policy. Export revalidates statistics and copies their numerical storage.
        flow_num_steps: Positive Python integer default for flow inference. Booleans
            are rejected. Validated even for MSE policies, which ignore it at sampling.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Inference steps are invalid, normalizer dimensions do not match,
            or stored statistics fail validation.
        OSError: A directory, temporary-file, replacement, or cleanup operation fails.
    """
    if (
        isinstance(flow_num_steps, bool)
        or not isinstance(flow_num_steps, int)
        or flow_num_steps <= 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("flow_num_steps must be a positive integer")

    normalizer.validate_dimensions(
        state_dim=model.config.state_dim,
        action_dim=model.config.action_dim,
    )

    checkpoint = {
        "format_version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
        "model_config": asdict(model.config),
        "model_state_dict": {
            name: tensor.detach().cpu() for name, tensor in model.state_dict().items()
        },
        "training_config": {"dropout": get_dropout_config(model)},
        "normalizer": normalizer.state_dict(),
        "inference_config": {
            "flow_num_steps": flow_num_steps,
        },
    }

    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    temporary_path = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
    try:
        torch.save(checkpoint, temporary_path)
        temporary_path.replace(path)
    finally:
        temporary_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

items.title: load_policy
items.text:
load_policy(path: Path | str, *, device: device | str = 'cpu') -> tuple[BasePolicy, Normalizer, dict[str, int]]

Reconstruct a checkpointed policy and return it in evaluation mode.

Load sequence

  1. Read tensors onto CPU with weights_only=True and check the format version.
  2. Reconstruct architecture and normalization statistics; validate dimensions and the saved positive integer flow-step default.
  3. Construct the model on meta, allocate CPU storage, and strictly load weights.
  4. Restore per-layer dropout, transfer to device, and call eval().

Model construction and loading do not consume default RNG streams. Inference randomness remains caller-owned and must be supplied when sampling actions. For further training, create a new optimizer and call model.train(); use override_dropout_p to replace saved dropout probabilities if desired.

The loader checks required components as it uses them rather than performing an exhaustive schema check up front. PyTorch deserialization and device errors propagate; no device fallback is attempted.

Parameters:

  • path (Path | str) –

    Checkpoint produced by save_policy.

  • device (device | str, default: 'cpu' ) –

    Destination device for the reconstructed policy. Normalizer arrays remain NumPy arrays on CPU.

Returns:

  • model ( BasePolicy ) –

    Loaded policy in evaluation mode on device.

  • normalizer ( Normalizer ) –

    Saved state/action statistics with independent copied storage.

  • inference_config ( dict[str, int] ) –

    Dictionary containing the validated flow_num_steps default.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    The outer object or format version is unsupported, architecture or normalization is invalid, flow steps are invalid, or dropout settings do not match the reconstructed model.

  • KeyError –

    A required checkpoint component is missing.

  • TypeError –

    Malformed architecture arguments or unsupported normalization tensor conversions fail. Other malformed inputs can also fail in PyTorch.

  • RuntimeError –

    Strict weight loading rejects missing, unexpected, or incompatible parameter entries, or a PyTorch operation fails.

  • OSError –

    The checkpoint file cannot be read.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/checkpoint.py 
def load_policy(
    path: Path | str,
    *,
    device: torch.device | str = "cpu",
) -> tuple[BasePolicy, Normalizer, dict[str, int]]:
    """Reconstruct a checkpointed policy and return it in evaluation mode.

    **Load sequence**

    1. Read tensors onto CPU with `weights_only=True` and check the format version.
    2. Reconstruct architecture and normalization statistics; validate dimensions
       and the saved positive integer flow-step default.
    3. Construct the model on meta, allocate CPU storage, and strictly load weights.
    4. Restore per-layer dropout, transfer to `device`, and call `eval()`.

    Model construction and loading do not consume default RNG streams. Inference
    randomness remains caller-owned and must be supplied when sampling actions.
    For further training, create a new optimizer and call `model.train()`; use
    [override_dropout_p][hw1_imitation.rng_modules.override_dropout_p] to replace
    saved dropout probabilities if desired.

    The loader checks required components as it uses them rather than performing
    an exhaustive schema check up front. PyTorch deserialization and device errors
    propagate; no device fallback is attempted.

    Args:
        path: Checkpoint produced by [save_policy][hw1_imitation.checkpoint.save_policy].
        device: Destination device for the reconstructed policy. Normalizer arrays
            remain NumPy arrays on CPU.

    Returns:
        model: Loaded policy in evaluation mode on `device`.
        normalizer: Saved state/action statistics with independent copied storage.
        inference_config: Dictionary containing the validated `flow_num_steps` default.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The outer object or format version is unsupported, architecture
            or normalization is invalid, flow steps are invalid, or dropout settings
            do not match the reconstructed model.
        KeyError: A required checkpoint component is missing.
        TypeError: Malformed architecture arguments or unsupported normalization
            tensor conversions fail. Other malformed inputs can also fail in PyTorch.
        RuntimeError: Strict weight loading rejects missing, unexpected, or
            incompatible parameter entries, or a PyTorch operation fails.
        OSError: The checkpoint file cannot be read.
    """
    checkpoint = torch.load(
        path,
        map_location="cpu",
        weights_only=True,
    )

    if (
        not isinstance(checkpoint, dict)
        or checkpoint.get("format_version") != CHECKPOINT_VERSION
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported checkpoint format; expected version {CHECKPOINT_VERSION}"
        )

    policy_config = PolicyConfig(**checkpoint["model_config"])
    normalizer = Normalizer.from_state_dict(checkpoint["normalizer"])
    normalizer.validate_dimensions(
        state_dim=policy_config.state_dim,
        action_dim=policy_config.action_dim,
    )

    flow_num_steps = checkpoint["inference_config"]["flow_num_steps"]
    if (
        isinstance(flow_num_steps, bool)
        or not isinstance(flow_num_steps, int)
        or flow_num_steps <= 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("Checkpoint flow_num_steps must be a positive integer")

    with torch.device("meta"):
        model = construct_policy(policy_config)

    model.to_empty(device="cpu")
    model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["model_state_dict"], strict=True)

    restore_dropout_config(model, checkpoint["training_config"]["dropout"])

    model = model.to(device=device)
    model.eval()

    return (
        model,
        normalizer,
        {
            "flow_num_steps": flow_num_steps,
        },
    )

items.title: data
items.text:
Load demonstrations and turn episode-local windows into training samples.

Data flow

  1. Use download_pusht if the data is not available locally. load_episodes_dataset reads the packed arrays into Episode objects exposed through EpisodesDataset.
  2. Split whole episodes into training and validation subsets. For a fresh run, fit Normalizer on training episodes only; when initializing from a checkpoint, reuse its stored normalizer. Use those same statistics for validation and inference.
  3. Build an EpisodeChunkDataset for each subset. It combines SingleEpisodeChunks children without crossing episode boundaries. Samples pair one state with an action window; optional padding repeats the episode's final action.

Storage and ownership

  • Episode arrays may share backing storage. Construction marks supplied arrays read-only, but writable aliases can still change their contents.
  • Chunk datasets may borrow that storage. Keep source data unchanged while using them.
  • Each sampled state/action pair contains independent float32 tensors.

items.title: Episode dataclass
items.text:
Store the aligned state-action arrays for one demonstration.

Each row pairs states[t] with actions[t].

Input requirements

  • Both arrays must be two-dimensional float32 arrays with matching, nonzero timestep counts.
  • Feature columns may be empty. Finite values and episode_id are not validated here.

Storage and ownership

  • Construction marks the supplied arrays read-only without copying data.
  • Frozen fields prevent rebinding, but writable aliases can still change the backing memory. This is not deeply immutable storage.
  • Keep the data unchanged while datasets use it.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    Either array is not two-dimensional, timestep counts differ, or there are no timesteps.

  • TypeError –

    Either array has a dtype other than float32.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/data.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Episode:
    """Store the aligned state-action arrays for one demonstration.

    Each row pairs `states[t]` with `actions[t]`.

    **Input requirements**

    - Both arrays must be two-dimensional float32 arrays with matching,
      nonzero timestep counts.
    - Feature columns may be empty. Finite values and `episode_id` are not
      validated here.

    **Storage and ownership**

    - Construction marks the supplied arrays read-only without copying data.
    - Frozen fields prevent rebinding, but writable aliases can still change
      the backing memory. This is not deeply immutable storage.
    - Keep the data unchanged while datasets use it.

    Attributes:
        episode_id: Caller-supplied identifier retained for dataset metadata.
            It need not equal the episode's position in a collection.
        states: State features with shape `(timesteps, state_dim)`, dtype
            float32. The supplied array object becomes read-only.
        actions: Actions with shape `(timesteps, action_dim)`, dtype float32.
            The supplied array object becomes read-only.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Either array is not two-dimensional, timestep counts differ,
            or there are no timesteps.
        TypeError: Either array has a dtype other than float32.
    """

    episode_id: int
    states: Float32Array  # shape: (timesteps, state_dim) - ReadOnly
    actions: Float32Array  # shape: (timesteps, action_dim) - ReadOnly

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate array shape and dtype, then mark both array objects read-only.

        This dataclass lifecycle hook runs on construction. Validation finishes
        before writeability flags are changed; no data is copied. Calling the hook
        again repeats these checks and flag updates.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Arrays are not two-dimensional, have different timestep
                counts, or contain no timesteps.
            TypeError: States or actions do not use float32.
        """
        if self.states.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"states should have shape: (timesteps, state_dim) but got {self.states.shape}"
            )

        if self.actions.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"actions should have shape: (timesteps, action_dim) but got {self.actions.shape}"
            )

        if len(self.states) != len(self.actions):
            raise ValueError("states and actions should be of same number of timesteps")

        if len(self.states) == 0:
            raise ValueError("episodes must have data for at least 1 timestamp")

        if self.actions.dtype != np.float32:
            raise TypeError(
                f"actions should have dtype:float32 but got {self.actions.dtype}"
            )

        if self.states.dtype != np.float32:
            raise TypeError(
                f"states should have dtype:float32 but got {self.states.dtype}"
            )

        # Make states and actions read_only.
        self.states.setflags(write=False)
        self.actions.setflags(write=False)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Return the number of aligned timesteps in the episode.

        Returns:
            count: Number of rows in `states`, which matches `actions` after
                successful construction.
        """
        return len(self.states)

items.title: EpisodesDataset
items.text:
Bases: Dataset[Episode]

Expose whole episodes through PyTorch's dataset interface.

Use this wrapper with utilities such as random_split. For training windows, use EpisodeChunkDataset.

Collection behavior

  • Store the supplied tuple by reference and return the same episode objects.
  • Perform no additional validation or copying; an empty collection is valid.

Implements the length and indexing interface of PyTorch Dataset.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/data.py 
class EpisodesDataset(Dataset[Episode]):
    """Expose whole episodes through PyTorch's dataset interface.

    Use this wrapper with utilities such as `random_split`. For training
    windows, use [EpisodeChunkDataset][hw1_imitation.data.EpisodeChunkDataset].

    **Collection behavior**

    - Store the supplied tuple by reference and return the same episode objects.
    - Perform no additional validation or copying; an empty collection is valid.

    Implements the length and indexing interface of
    [PyTorch Dataset](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html#torch.utils.data.Dataset).

    Attributes:
        episodes: The original ordered tuple of episode objects. Array ownership
            and writeability remain those of each episode.
    """
    def __init__(self, episodes: tuple[Episode, ...]):
        """Retain the episode collection without validating or copying it.

        Args:
            episodes: Ordered tuple to expose through the dataset. Empty tuples are
                valid; element types are assumed to match the annotation.
        """
        self.episodes = episodes

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Return the number of episodes in the stored collection.

        Returns:
            count: Length of `episodes`, including zero for an empty collection.
        """
        return len(self.episodes)

    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Episode:
        """Delegate episode lookup to the stored tuple.

        Args:
            idx: Integer position, with negative indices counted from the end.
                Although annotated for integer lookup, the implementation also
                passes slices through to the tuple unchanged.

        Returns:
            episode: The same stored episode object for an integer index. A slice
                returns a tuple of the original episode objects instead; no arrays
                are copied.

        Raises:
            IndexError: An integer index is outside the tuple's bounds.
            TypeError: The tuple rejects the index type.
        """
        return self.episodes[idx]

items.title: Normalizer dataclass
items.text:
Normalize state and action features using stored means and scales.

Typical use

  1. Fit training observations with from_packed_data or from_episodes_data. Reuse those statistics for validation and inference.
  2. Standardize states and actions with normalize_state and normalize_action.
  3. Restore policy outputs to action coordinates with denormalize_action.

Storage and validation

  • Direct construction borrows all four arrays without copying or changing their writeability. Frozen fields prevent rebinding, not array mutation.
  • Construction validates statistics; transformations do not revalidate them.
  • state_dict and from_state_dict copy storage for checkpoints.

See from_episodes_data for a worked example.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    Statistics are empty, not matching one-dimensional vectors, contain nonfinite values, or have nonpositive scales.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/data.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Normalizer:
    """Normalize state and action features using stored means and scales.

    **Typical use**

    1. Fit training observations with
       [from_packed_data][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer.from_packed_data] or
       [from_episodes_data][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer.from_episodes_data].
       Reuse those statistics for validation and inference.
    2. Standardize states and actions with
       [normalize_state][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer.normalize_state] and
       [normalize_action][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer.normalize_action].
    3. Restore policy outputs to action coordinates with
       [denormalize_action][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer.denormalize_action].

    **Storage and validation**

    - Direct construction borrows all four arrays without copying or changing
      their writeability. Frozen fields prevent rebinding, not array mutation.
    - Construction validates statistics; transformations do not revalidate them.
    - [state_dict][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer.state_dict] and
      [from_state_dict][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer.from_state_dict] copy
      storage for checkpoints.

    See [from_episodes_data][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer.from_episodes_data]
    for a worked example.

    Attributes:
        state_mean: Finite per-feature state means, shape `(state_dim,)`.
        state_std: Finite, strictly positive state scales, matching `state_mean`.
        action_mean: Finite per-feature action means, shape `(action_dim,)`.
        action_std: Finite, strictly positive action scales, matching `action_mean`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Statistics are empty, not matching one-dimensional vectors,
            contain nonfinite values, or have nonpositive scales.
    """

    state_mean: np.ndarray
    state_std: np.ndarray
    action_mean: np.ndarray
    action_std: np.ndarray

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate statistics after dataclass construction.

        This lifecycle hook also runs when a factory constructs an instance.
        It neither copies nor freezes array storage.

        Raises:
            ValueError: A statistics vector is malformed or has invalid values.
        """
        self._validate_statistics()

    def normalize_state(self, state: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Standardize states by subtracting the mean and dividing by the scale.

        Args:
            state: State array, normally shaped `(..., state_dim)`. NumPy
                broadcasting determines compatible shapes; rank, feature count,
                dtype, and finite values are not checked explicitly.

        Returns:
            result: A newly computed array with the broadcast result shape. The input and
                stored statistics are not modified; NumPy determines the result dtype.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Input and statistics cannot be broadcast together.
        """
        return (state - self.state_mean) / self.state_std

    def normalize_action(self, action: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Standardize actions by subtracting the mean and dividing by the scale.

        Args:
            action: Action array, normally shaped `(..., action_dim)`. NumPy
                broadcasting determines compatibility; rank, feature count, dtype,
                and finite values are not checked explicitly.

        Returns:
            result: A newly computed array with the broadcast result shape. The input and
                stored statistics are not modified; NumPy determines the result dtype.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Input and statistics cannot be broadcast together.
        """
        return (action - self.action_mean) / self.action_std

    def denormalize_action(self, action: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Restore action coordinates by multiplying by the scale and adding the mean.

        Args:
            action: Normalized action array, normally shaped `(..., action_dim)`.
                NumPy broadcasting determines compatibility; inputs are not
                explicitly checked for rank, feature count, dtype, or finite values.

        Returns:
            result: A newly computed array in the original action coordinates, with the
                broadcast result shape. Inputs and statistics are not modified.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Input and statistics cannot be broadcast together.
        """
        return action * self.action_std + self.action_mean

    @property
    def state_dim(self):
        """Return the number of state features in the stored mean vector.

        Returns:
            count (int): Number of entries in `state_mean`.
        """
        return self.state_mean.shape[0]

    @property
    def action_dim(self):
        """Return the number of action features in the stored mean vector.

        Returns:
            count (int): Number of entries in `action_mean`.
        """
        return self.action_mean.shape[0]

    @staticmethod
    def _safe_std(std: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-6) -> np.ndarray:
        """Clamp scales from below without modifying the input (implementation detail).

        Args:
            std: Array of per-feature scales computed by a fitting method.
            eps: Lower bound applied elementwise. Positivity is assumed, not checked.

        Returns:
            result: A new array containing `maximum(std, eps)`. NaNs remain NaN and are
                rejected by subsequent construction validation.
        """
        return np.maximum(std, eps)

    @classmethod
    def from_packed_data(
        cls,
        states: np.ndarray,
        actions: np.ndarray,
    ) -> "Normalizer":
        """Fit feature statistics across the leading axis of packed training arrays.

        - Compute means and population standard deviations (`ddof=0`) using
          NumPy's input-dtype rules.
        - Clamp scales to at least `1e-6`, including constant features.
        - Leave inputs unchanged; computed statistics have independent storage.

        Args:
            states: Training states, intended shape `(timesteps, state_dim)`.
            actions: Training actions, intended shape `(timesteps, action_dim)`.
                Equal timestep counts and two-dimensional inputs are assumptions,
                not explicit checks; each array is reduced independently.

        Returns:
            result: A normalizer containing the computed feature statistics.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Reduced statistics are not matching nonempty vectors or
                contain invalid values. Empty or nonfinite inputs can also emit
                NumPy warnings before validation fails.
        """
        state_mean = states.mean(axis=0)
        state_std = cls._safe_std(states.std(axis=0))
        action_mean = actions.mean(axis=0)
        action_std = cls._safe_std(actions.std(axis=0))
        return cls(state_mean, state_std, action_mean, action_std)

    @classmethod
    def from_episodes_data(
        cls, episodes: Sequence[Episode] | Dataset[Episode]
    ) -> "Normalizer":
        """Fit statistics over all timesteps in a nonempty collection of episodes.

        Concatenate episodes, then delegate to
        [from_packed_data][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer.from_packed_data].

        - Longer episodes contribute more samples to the fit.
        - Concatenation allocates combined state/action arrays.
        - Episode arrays are neither modified nor retained as statistics.

        Args:
            episodes: Iterable sequence or dataset of episodes with compatible
                state feature dimensions and compatible action feature dimensions.

        Returns:
            result: A normalizer fitted to the concatenated demonstration data.

        Raises:
            ValueError: No episodes are supplied, feature shapes cannot be
                concatenated, or the resulting statistics fail validation.

        Examples:
            Fit only on training data and reuse the resulting statistics:

            ```python
            normalizer = Normalizer.from_episodes_data(training_episodes)
            normalized_states = normalizer.normalize_state(episode.states)
            normalized_actions = normalizer.normalize_action(episode.actions)
            actions = normalizer.denormalize_action(normalized_actions)
            ```
        """
        states = [episode.states for episode in episodes]
        actions = [episode.actions for episode in episodes]

        if len(states) == 0 or len(actions) == 0:
            raise ValueError("Normalization requires at least one episode.")

        states = np.concatenate(states, axis=0)
        actions = np.concatenate(actions, axis=0)
        return cls.from_packed_data(states=states, actions=actions)

    def state_dict(self) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """Export independent CPU tensors for the checkpoint schema.

        Revalidate statistics before export, since their arrays can have been
        mutated after construction. Each returned tensor owns copied numerical
        storage relative to this normalizer.

        Returns:
            result: Mapping with `state_mean`, `state_std`, `action_mean`, and `action_std`.
                Tensor shapes and supported NumPy dtypes are preserved.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Stored statistics no longer pass validation.
            TypeError: A statistics dtype is unsupported by `torch.from_numpy`.
        """
        self._validate_statistics()
        return {
            "state_mean": torch.from_numpy(self.state_mean.copy()),
            "state_std": torch.from_numpy(self.state_std.copy()),
            "action_mean": torch.from_numpy(self.action_mean.copy()),
            "action_std": torch.from_numpy(self.action_std.copy()),
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_state_dict(cls, state: dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> "Normalizer":
        """Restore statistics without sharing checkpoint tensor storage.

        Detach each tensor, move it to CPU, convert it to NumPy, and copy it.
        Construction validates the restored arrays.

        **Checkpoint schema**

        - Require the four keys listed below; ignore extra keys.
        - Coordinate schema changes with the outer checkpoint version.

        Args:
            state: Tensor mapping containing `state_mean`, `state_std`,
                `action_mean`, and `action_std`. Tensors must support NumPy conversion.

        Returns:
            result: A normalizer whose statistics are independent copies of the tensors.

        Raises:
            KeyError: A required key is absent.
            ValueError: Restored statistics fail construction validation.
            TypeError: A tensor dtype or layout cannot be converted to NumPy.
            RuntimeError: PyTorch rejects a tensor conversion, such as unresolved
                conjugate or negative flags.
        """

        def to_array(name: str) -> np.ndarray:
            """Copy one checkpoint tensor into an independent NumPy array.

            This function-local helper detaches the tensor, moves it to CPU, converts it
            to NumPy, and copies the result. It does not itself validate statistics.

            Args:
                name: Required key in the enclosing checkpoint `state` mapping.

            Returns:
                array: Independent NumPy storage with the converted tensor's shape and dtype.

            Raises:
                KeyError: The requested entry is missing.
                TypeError: The tensor dtype or layout cannot be converted to NumPy.
                RuntimeError: PyTorch rejects a device transfer or tensor conversion.
            """
            return state[name].detach().cpu().numpy().copy()

        return cls(
            state_mean=to_array("state_mean"),
            state_std=to_array("state_std"),
            action_mean=to_array("action_mean"),
            action_std=to_array("action_std"),
        )

    def validate_dimensions(
        self,
        *,
        state_dim: int,
        action_dim: int,
    ) -> None:
        """Check statistics against the policy's expected feature dimensions.

        Only shapes are checked. This does not revalidate finite values or positive
        scales and does not modify the arrays.

        Args:
            state_dim: Expected number of state features.
            action_dim: Expected number of action features.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Any statistics array has a shape different from its
                expected one-dimensional feature shape.
        """
        expected_shapes = (
            ("state_mean", self.state_mean, (state_dim,)),
            ("state_std", self.state_std, (state_dim,)),
            ("action_mean", self.action_mean, (action_dim,)),
            ("action_std", self.action_std, (action_dim,)),
        )

        for name, values, expected in expected_shapes:
            if values.shape != expected:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{name} must have shape {expected}, got {values.shape}"
                )

    def _validate_statistics(self) -> None:
        """Check vector shapes and finite values (implementation detail).

        Each mean must be a nonempty vector with a matching scale vector; scales
        must be strictly positive. No dtype requirement or copying is imposed.

        Raises:
            ValueError: A shape, finiteness, or positive-scale requirement fails.
        """
        for name, mean, std in (
            ("state", self.state_mean, self.state_std),
            ("action", self.action_mean, self.action_std),
        ):
            if mean.ndim != 1 or mean.size == 0 or std.shape != mean.shape:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} statistics must be matching nonempty vectors")
            if not np.isfinite(mean).all():
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid normalization statistics: {name}_mean")
            if not np.isfinite(std).all() or (std <= 0).any():
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid normalization statistics: {name}_std")

def validate_dimensions(
    self,
    *,
    state_dim: int,
    action_dim: int,
) -> None:
    """Check statistics against the policy's expected feature dimensions.

    Only shapes are checked. This does not revalidate finite values or positive
    scales and does not modify the arrays.

    Args:
        state_dim: Expected number of state features.
        action_dim: Expected number of action features.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Any statistics array has a shape different from its
            expected one-dimensional feature shape.
    """
    expected_shapes = (
        ("state_mean", self.state_mean, (state_dim,)),
        ("state_std", self.state_std, (state_dim,)),
        ("action_mean", self.action_mean, (action_dim,)),
        ("action_std", self.action_std, (action_dim,)),
    )

    for name, values, expected in expected_shapes:
        if values.shape != expected:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{name} must have shape {expected}, got {values.shape}"
            )

def _validate_statistics(self) -> None:
    """Check vector shapes and finite values (implementation detail).

    Each mean must be a nonempty vector with a matching scale vector; scales
    must be strictly positive. No dtype requirement or copying is imposed.

    Raises:
        ValueError: A shape, finiteness, or positive-scale requirement fails.
    """
    for name, mean, std in (
        ("state", self.state_mean, self.state_std),
        ("action", self.action_mean, self.action_std),
    ):
        if mean.ndim != 1 or mean.size == 0 or std.shape != mean.shape:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} statistics must be matching nonempty vectors")
        if not np.isfinite(mean).all():
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid normalization statistics: {name}_mean")
        if not np.isfinite(std).all() or (std <= 0).any():
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid normalization statistics: {name}_std")

Expose one episode as current-state and future-action training samples.

At timestep t, a sample pairs states[t] with actions beginning at t.

Window rules

  • Without padding, only complete windows exist. The dataset length is max(0, timesteps - chunk_length + 1).
  • With padding, every original timestep is a valid start. Windows past the end repeat the final action; padding creates no extra start positions.
  • Optional normalization runs once during construction, before padding.

Storage and ownership

  • Borrow episode arrays when no transformation is needed. Normalization allocates new state/action arrays; padding allocates a new action array.
  • Keep source episode arrays unchanged for this dataset's lifetime.
  • Each lookup returns independent float32 tensors. Changing a returned sample does not affect source arrays or later samples.

Implements PyTorch Dataset. Use EpisodeChunkDataset to combine episodes without crossing boundaries.

class SingleEpisodeChunks(Dataset[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]):
    """Expose one episode as current-state and future-action training samples.

    At timestep `t`, a sample pairs `states[t]` with actions beginning at `t`.

    **Window rules**

    - Without padding, only complete windows exist. The dataset length is
      `max(0, timesteps - chunk_length + 1)`.
    - With padding, every original timestep is a valid start. Windows past the
      end repeat the final action; padding creates no extra start positions.
    - Optional normalization runs once during construction, before padding.

    **Storage and ownership**

    - Borrow episode arrays when no transformation is needed. Normalization
      allocates new state/action arrays; padding allocates a new action array.
    - Keep source episode arrays unchanged for this dataset's lifetime.
    - Each lookup returns independent float32 tensors. Changing a returned
      sample does not affect source arrays or later samples.

    Implements [PyTorch Dataset](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html#torch.utils.data.Dataset).
    Use [EpisodeChunkDataset][hw1_imitation.data.EpisodeChunkDataset] to combine
    episodes without crossing boundaries.

    Attributes:
        _chunk_length: Implementation detail: positive number of actions in
            each sample, retained from the constructor.
        _length: Implementation detail: number of valid sample starts, computed
            once from episode length, chunk length and padding mode.
        _states: Implementation detail: state rows used for lookup. Borrowed
            from the episode or independently computed by normalization.
        _actions: Implementation detail: action rows used for windows. Borrowed
            unless normalization or padding allocates a replacement array.
        _episode_id: Implementation detail: original episode identifier exposed
            by the `episode_id` property.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        episode: Episode,
        *,
        chunk_length: int,
        pad_action_chunk: bool = False,
        normalizer: Normalizer | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Prepare episode-local windows, optionally normalizing and padding once.

        1. If supplied, check the normalizer's dimensions against the episode
           and normalize the arrays. Statistics are not revalidated for finite
           or positive values here.
        2. If requested, pad with the final action after normalization.

        Neither source array is modified; the normalizer itself is not retained.

        Args:
            episode: Demonstration supplying aligned state/action arrays and its ID.
            chunk_length: Positive Python integer specifying actions per window.
                Boolean values are explicitly rejected.
            pad_action_chunk: Whether to repeat the final action so every episode
                timestep has a complete window.
            normalizer: Statistics to apply to the episode's states and actions.
                `None` leaves them in their original coordinates.

        Raises:
            TypeError: `chunk_length` is not a Python integer or is a boolean.
            ValueError: `chunk_length` is not positive, or the normalizer's state
                or action dimensions differ from the episode's.
        """
        if isinstance(chunk_length, bool) or not isinstance(chunk_length, int):
            raise TypeError("chunk_length must be an integer")
        if chunk_length <= 0:
            raise ValueError("chunk_length must be positive")

        states, actions = episode.states, episode.actions

        # These transformations produce new arrays without modifying
        # the episode. Compute them once, rather than for every window.
        if normalizer is not None:
            # Validate dimensions.
            normalizer.validate_dimensions(
                state_dim=states.shape[1],
                action_dim=actions.shape[1],
            )
            (states, actions) = (
                normalizer.normalize_state(states),
                normalizer.normalize_action(actions),
            )

        if pad_action_chunk and chunk_length > 1:
            # Append enough actions for a chunk starting at the final
            # timestep. Padding does not create additional sample starts.
            actions = np.pad(
                array=actions,
                pad_width=((0, chunk_length - 1), (0, 0)),
                mode="edge",
            )

        self._chunk_length = chunk_length
        self._length = (
            len(episode)
            if pad_action_chunk
            else max(0, len(episode) - chunk_length + 1)
        )
        self._states = states
        self._actions = actions
        self._episode_id = episode.episode_id

    @property
    def state_dim(self) -> int:
        """Return the feature count of the prepared state rows.

        Returns:
            count: Number of columns in `_states`.
        """
        return self._states.shape[1]

    @property
    def action_dim(self) -> int:
        """Return the feature count of the prepared action rows.

        Returns:
            count: Number of columns in `_actions`.
        """
        return self._actions.shape[1]

    @property
    def episode_id(self) -> int:
        """Return the original episode's identifier.

        Returns:
            identifier: Identifier copied from the episode during construction;
                it is not inferred from an index or validated here.
        """
        return self._episode_id

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Return the number of valid window starts.

        Returns:
            count: Stored sample count. This can be zero when the episode is shorter
                than the chunk length and padding is disabled.
        """
        return self._length

    def __getitem__(
        self,
        index: int,
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        # Handle -ve index : wrap around.
        """Copy one current-state and action-window pair into float32 tensors.

        Args:
            index: Integer start position. Negative indices count from the end of
                this dataset's valid starts; slices are not supported.

        Returns:
            sample: A pair containing a state tensor shaped `(state_dim,)` and an
                action tensor shaped `(chunk_length, action_dim)`. Both are new
                float32 tensors independent of stored arrays and other samples.
                Coordinates are normalized only if a normalizer was supplied.

        Raises:
            IndexError: The index is outside `[-len(self), len(self))`; every index
                fails when this dataset is empty. NumPy also raises IndexError for
                unsupported scalar indices such as an in-range float.
            TypeError: An index such as a slice cannot be compared with integers,
                or an unsupported type reaches NumPy slicing.
        """
        if index < 0:
            index += self._length
        if not 0 <= index < self._length:
            raise IndexError("index out of bound")

        chunk_end = index + self._chunk_length

        state = self._states[index]
        action_chunk = self._actions[index:chunk_end]

        return (
            torch.tensor(data=state, dtype=torch.float32),
            torch.tensor(data=action_chunk, dtype=torch.float32),
        )

Bases: ConcatDataset[tuple[Tensor, Tensor]]

Concatenate episode-local training windows without crossing boundaries.

Construction rules

  • Build one SingleEpisodeChunks child per episode, in input order.
  • Require matching state and action feature dimensions across all children.
  • Allow unpadded short episodes to contribute zero samples, provided at least one valid sample remains in the combined dataset.

Indexing and ownership

  • PyTorch ConcatDataset supplies __len__, __getitem__, the child datasets collection, and cumulative index routing. Those implementations are not repeated here.
  • Valid negative indices count from the combined dataset's end. In the installed implementation, indices below -len(self) raise ValueError; nonnegative indices at or above len(self) raise IndexError.
  • Children borrow arrays or compute replacements as described by SingleEpisodeChunks; the episodes are not copied wholesale. Keep source storage unchanged while using the dataset.
  • Returned state/action tensors are independent float32 copies.

See constructor for a worked construction example.

class EpisodeChunkDataset(ConcatDataset[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]):
    """Concatenate episode-local training windows without crossing boundaries.

    **Construction rules**

    - Build one [SingleEpisodeChunks][hw1_imitation.data.SingleEpisodeChunks]
      child per episode, in input order.
    - Require matching state and action feature dimensions across all children.
    - Allow unpadded short episodes to contribute zero samples, provided at
      least one valid sample remains in the combined dataset.

    **Indexing and ownership**

    - [PyTorch ConcatDataset](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html#torch.utils.data.ConcatDataset)
      supplies `__len__`, `__getitem__`, the child `datasets` collection, and
      cumulative index routing. Those implementations are not repeated here.
    - Valid negative indices count from the combined dataset's end. In the
      installed implementation, indices below `-len(self)` raise `ValueError`;
      nonnegative indices at or above `len(self)` raise `IndexError`.
    - Children borrow arrays or compute replacements as described by
      `SingleEpisodeChunks`; the episodes are not copied wholesale. Keep source
      storage unchanged while using the dataset.
    - Returned state/action tensors are independent float32 copies.

    See [constructor][hw1_imitation.data.EpisodeChunkDataset.__init__] for a worked
    construction example.

    Attributes:
        _state_dim: Implementation detail: state feature count shared by all
            children and exposed through `state_dim`.
        _action_dim: Implementation detail: action feature count shared by all
            children and exposed through `action_dim`.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        episodes: Sequence[Episode] | Dataset[Episode],
        *,
        chunk_length: int,
        normalizer: Normalizer | None = None,
        pad_action_chunk: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Construct compatible child datasets and require a nonempty combined result.

        - Each child applies normalization and padding independently.
        - Check dimensions even for episodes that produce zero windows.
        - Iterate the input sequence once and retain the child datasets, not
          the original sequence.

        Args:
            episodes: Nonempty sequence or dataset of episodes in concatenation order.
            chunk_length: Positive Python integer specifying actions per window.
                Passed to every child; boolean values are rejected.
            normalizer: Shared statistics applied to every child, or `None` for
                original state/action coordinates. Feature dimensions must match.
            pad_action_chunk: Whether each child repeats its own final action to
                complete windows beginning near its end.

        Raises:
            ValueError: No episodes are supplied, episode dimensions disagree,
                a child rejects the chunk length or normalizer dimensions, or no
                valid windows remain after all children are constructed.
            TypeError: A child rejects a non-integer or boolean chunk length.

        Examples:
            Fit statistics on the training subset, then construct normalized windows
            from that same subset:

            ```python
            normalizer = Normalizer.from_episodes_data(training_episodes)
            windows = EpisodeChunkDataset(
                training_episodes, chunk_length=8, normalizer=normalizer,
                pad_action_chunk=True,
            )
            state, actions = windows[0]
            ```
        """
        children = []
        expected_dimensions: tuple[int, int] | None = None

        for episode in episodes:
            dimensions = (
                episode.states.shape[1],
                episode.actions.shape[1],
            )

            if expected_dimensions is None:
                expected_dimensions = dimensions
            elif dimensions != expected_dimensions:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"episode {episode.episode_id} has state/action dimensions "
                    f"{dimensions}; expected {expected_dimensions}"
                )

            children.append(
                SingleEpisodeChunks(
                    episode,
                    chunk_length=chunk_length,
                    normalizer=normalizer,
                    pad_action_chunk=pad_action_chunk,
                )
            )

        if expected_dimensions is None:
            raise ValueError("at least one episode is required")

        self._state_dim, self._action_dim = expected_dimensions

        super().__init__(children)

        if len(self) == 0:
            raise ValueError("no valid chunks: reduce chunk_length or enable padding")

    @property
    def state_dim(self) -> int:
        """Return the state feature count shared by every child dataset.

        Returns:
            count: State dimension recorded during construction.
        """
        return self._state_dim

    @property
    def action_dim(self) -> int:
        """Return the action feature count shared by every child dataset.

        Returns:
            count: Action dimension recorded during construction.
        """
        return self._action_dim

download_pusht(dataset_dir: Path) -> Path

Download the Push-T archive when needed and extract it locally.

Cache behavior

  1. Create dataset_dir and check the expected Zarr path.
  2. If that path exists, return immediately without validating its type or data.
  3. Otherwise reuse an existing pusht.zip, or download it from PUSHT_URL, then extract the archive into dataset_dir.

This helper does not validate archive contents, verify a checksum, or repair partial downloads. Download/extraction failures propagate and may leave partial files; neither the archive nor extracted data is removed afterward.

Parameters:

  • dataset_dir (Path) –

    Root directory for the cached ZIP and extracted dataset.

Returns:

  • zarr_path ( Path ) –

    Expected extracted Zarr path under dataset_dir. Its existence or validity is not checked again after extraction.

Raises:

  • OSError –

    Directory creation, download, or file access fails.

  • BadZipFile –

    The cached or downloaded archive is not a valid ZIP.

Other network and extraction errors propagate from their underlying libraries.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/data.py 
def download_pusht(dataset_dir: Path) -> Path:
    """Download the Push-T archive when needed and extract it locally.

    **Cache behavior**

    1. Create `dataset_dir` and check the expected Zarr path.
    2. If that path exists, return immediately without validating its type or data.
    3. Otherwise reuse an existing `pusht.zip`, or download it from `PUSHT_URL`,
       then extract the archive into `dataset_dir`.

    This helper does not validate archive contents, verify a checksum, or repair
    partial downloads. Download/extraction failures propagate and may leave partial
    files; neither the archive nor extracted data is removed afterward.

    Args:
        dataset_dir: Root directory for the cached ZIP and extracted dataset.

    Returns:
        zarr_path: Expected extracted Zarr path under `dataset_dir`. Its existence
            or validity is not checked again after extraction.

    Raises:
        OSError: Directory creation, download, or file access fails.
        zipfile.BadZipFile: The cached or downloaded archive is not a valid ZIP.

    Other network and extraction errors propagate from their underlying libraries.
    """
    dataset_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    zarr_path = dataset_dir / ZARR_RELATIVE_PATH
    # check if the final extracted path exists
    # exit early if final path exists
    # BUG: path might exist without final data
    # need some real data based checks.
    if zarr_path.exists():
        return zarr_path

    zip_path = dataset_dir / "pusht.zip"
    if not zip_path.exists():
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(PUSHT_URL, zip_path)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "r") as zip_ref:
        zip_ref.extractall(dataset_dir)

    return zarr_path

Materialize packed Push-T arrays from a Zarr group (implementation detail).

Open the group read-only and load data/state, data/action, and meta/episode_ends. Convert these to NumPy arrays in memory; returned arrays are not live views into the Zarr store. Shape and episode-boundary checks are performed later by the episode-construction helper.

Parameters:

  • zarr_path (Path) –

    Extracted Push-T Zarr group to open.

Returns:

  • states ( ndarray ) –

    Float32 array of concatenated state rows across all episodes.

  • actions ( ndarray ) –

    Float32 array of concatenated action rows across all episodes.

  • episode_ends ( ndarray ) –

    Int64 array of exclusive episode-end offsets. Conversion to int64 occurs here, before subsequent boundary validation.

Raises:

  • KeyError –

    A required array path is missing from the group.

  • AssertionError –

    A required object is not a zarr.Array, when Python assertions are enabled.

Zarr storage and NumPy conversion errors propagate.

def _load_pusht_zarr(zarr_path: Path) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Materialize packed Push-T arrays from a Zarr group (implementation detail).

    Open the group read-only and load `data/state`, `data/action`, and
    `meta/episode_ends`. Convert these to NumPy arrays in memory; returned arrays
    are not live views into the Zarr store. Shape and episode-boundary checks are
    performed later by the episode-construction helper.

    Args:
        zarr_path: Extracted Push-T Zarr group to open.

    Returns:
        states: Float32 array of concatenated state rows across all episodes.
        actions: Float32 array of concatenated action rows across all episodes.
        episode_ends: Int64 array of exclusive episode-end offsets. Conversion to
            int64 occurs here, before subsequent boundary validation.

    Raises:
        KeyError: A required array path is missing from the group.
        AssertionError: A required object is not a `zarr.Array`, when Python
            assertions are enabled.

    Zarr storage and NumPy conversion errors propagate.
    """
    root = zarr.open_group(zarr_path, mode="r")
    states_array = root["data/state"]
    actions_array = root["data/action"]
    episode_ends_array = root["meta/episode_ends"]

    assert isinstance(states_array, zarr.Array)
    assert isinstance(actions_array, zarr.Array)
    assert isinstance(episode_ends_array, zarr.Array)

    states = np.asarray(states_array, dtype=np.float32)  # 25650x5
    actions = np.asarray(actions_array, dtype=np.float32)  # 25650x2
    episode_ends = np.asarray(episode_ends_array, dtype=np.int64)  # 206x1
    return states, actions, episode_ends

items.title: _get_episodes_from_packed_data
items.text:
_get_episodes_from_packed_data(states: Float32Array, actions: Float32Array, episode_ends: NDArray[int64]) -> tuple[Episode, ...]

Expose packed data as read-only episode views (implementation detail).

Validate exclusive boundaries, then slice arrays in source order and assign zero-based episode IDs. Each Episode validates its slice and marks that view read-only. The input arrays' own writeability flags are not changed; writable aliases can still mutate shared backing data.

Parameters:

  • states (Float32Array) –

    Float32 states shaped (total_timesteps, state_dim).

  • actions (Float32Array) –

    Float32 actions shaped (total_timesteps, action_dim).

  • episode_ends (NDArray[int64]) –

    Nonempty one-dimensional integer array. Offsets must be positive, strictly increasing, and end at total_timesteps.

Returns:

  • episodes ( tuple[Episode, ...] ) –

    Tuple of episodes in source order, sharing numerical storage with the input arrays. No per-episode data copy is made.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    Packed lengths differ, boundary rank/order/coverage is invalid, or an episode's shape or timestep count is invalid.

  • TypeError –

    Boundary dtype is not integer or episode arrays are not float32.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/data.py 
def _get_episodes_from_packed_data(
    states: Float32Array,
    actions: Float32Array,
    episode_ends: NDArray[np.int64],
) -> tuple[Episode, ...]:
    """Expose packed data as read-only episode views (implementation detail).

    Validate exclusive boundaries, then slice arrays in source order and assign
    zero-based episode IDs. Each `Episode` validates its slice and marks that view
    read-only. The input arrays' own writeability flags are not changed; writable
    aliases can still mutate shared backing data.

    Args:
        states: Float32 states shaped `(total_timesteps, state_dim)`.
        actions: Float32 actions shaped `(total_timesteps, action_dim)`.
        episode_ends: Nonempty one-dimensional integer array. Offsets must be
            positive, strictly increasing, and end at `total_timesteps`.

    Returns:
        episodes: Tuple of episodes in source order, sharing numerical storage with
            the input arrays. No per-episode data copy is made.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Packed lengths differ, boundary rank/order/coverage is invalid,
            or an episode's shape or timestep count is invalid.
        TypeError: Boundary dtype is not integer or episode arrays are not float32.
    """
    if len(states) != len(actions):
        raise ValueError("packed states and actions must have equal lengths")

    if episode_ends.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError("episode_ends must be one-dimensional")

    if not np.issubdtype(episode_ends.dtype, np.integer):
        raise TypeError("episode_ends must contain integers")

    if len(episode_ends) == 0:
        raise ValueError("the dataset must contain at least one episode")

    if episode_ends[0] <= 0 or np.any(episode_ends[1:] <= episode_ends[:-1]):
        raise ValueError("episode ends must be positive and strictly increasing")

    if episode_ends[-1] != len(states):
        raise ValueError("the last episode must end at the end of the data")

    episode_start = 0
    episodes = []
    for episode_id, episode_end in enumerate(episode_ends):
        episode = Episode(
            episode_id=episode_id,
            states=states[episode_start:episode_end],
            actions=actions[episode_start:episode_end],
        )
        episodes.append(episode)
        episode_start = episode_end
    return tuple(episodes)

Load Push-T arrays once and expose them as read-only episode views.

Materialize the full state/action data, split it at validated episode ends, and wrap the resulting episodes in EpisodesDataset. Slices retain the backing arrays after this function returns, avoiding per-episode copies.

Ordinary writes through episode arrays are rejected. This protects against accidental mutation, not changes through other writable aliases.

Returns:

    Dataset of episodes in source order, with zero-based episode IDs and shared backing arrays.

Raises:

    Loaded shapes, lengths, or episode boundaries fail validation.

  • TypeError –

    Episode arrays or boundary dtype fail the downstream checks.

  • KeyError –

    A required Zarr array path is absent.

Storage/conversion errors and the helper's enabled type assertions propagate.

def load_episodes_dataset(zarr_path: Path) -> EpisodesDataset:
    """Load Push-T arrays once and expose them as read-only episode views.

    Materialize the full state/action data, split it at validated episode ends,
    and wrap the resulting episodes in `EpisodesDataset`. Slices retain the backing
    arrays after this function returns, avoiding per-episode copies.

    Ordinary writes through episode arrays are rejected. This protects against
    accidental mutation, not changes through other writable aliases.

    Args:
        zarr_path: Extracted Push-T Zarr group containing packed states, actions,
            and exclusive episode-end offsets.

    Returns:
        dataset: Dataset of episodes in source order, with zero-based episode IDs
            and shared backing arrays.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Loaded shapes, lengths, or episode boundaries fail validation.
        TypeError: Episode arrays or boundary dtype fail the downstream checks.
        KeyError: A required Zarr array path is absent.

    Storage/conversion errors and the helper's enabled type assertions propagate.
    """
    states, actions, episode_ends = _load_pusht_zarr(zarr_path=zarr_path)
    # Basic slices share storage; Episode makes these slices read-only.
    return EpisodesDataset(
        _get_episodes_from_packed_data(
            states=states,
            actions=actions,
            episode_ends=episode_ends,
        )
    )

items.title: early_stopping
items.text:
Detect plateaus in an evaluation metric.

Use EarlyStopping to decide when to stop training. Call update once per evaluation and let the training loop act on its result.

The training driver maximizes mean evaluation reward. It converts warm-up epochs into optimizer steps, while patience counts evaluation calls.

items.title: ObjectiveType module-attribute
items.text: ObjectiveType = Literal['min', 'max']

items.title: EarlyStopping dataclass
items.text:
Request stopping after too many evaluations without sufficient improvement.

How it works

  • The first finite observation establishes a reference, even during warm-up.
  • An improvement must strictly exceed min_delta in the chosen direction. It replaces the reference and resets the stale-evaluation counter.
  • Otherwise, increment the counter only when step > start_step. Return True when the counter reaches patience.

Important behavior

  • Small gains can accumulate against the last reference, not the previous value.
  • Patience counts stale evaluations, not optimizer steps or epochs.
  • A stop signal is not latched: a later sufficient improvement clears it. The caller decides whether to exit the training loop.
  • Checkpoint selection is separate and can retain a better score even when its improvement is too small to reset patience.

See update for a worked example.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/early_stopping.py 
@dataclass
class EarlyStopping:
    """Request stopping after too many evaluations without sufficient improvement.

    **How it works**

    - The first finite observation establishes a reference, even during warm-up.
    - An improvement must strictly exceed `min_delta` in the chosen direction.
      It replaces the reference and resets the stale-evaluation counter.
    - Otherwise, increment the counter only when `step > start_step`.
      Return `True` when the counter reaches `patience`.

    **Important behavior**

    - Small gains can accumulate against the last reference, not the previous
      value.
    - Patience counts stale evaluations, not optimizer steps or epochs.
    - A stop signal is not latched: a later sufficient improvement clears it.
      The caller decides whether to exit the training loop.
    - Checkpoint selection is separate and can retain a better score even when
      its improvement is too small to reset patience.

    See [update][hw1_imitation.early_stopping.EarlyStopping.update] for a worked
    example.

    Attributes:
        patience: Positive number of stale evaluation updates needed to request
            stopping. This counts calls after warm-up, not elapsed optimizer
            steps or epochs.
        min_delta: Finite, nonnegative improvement threshold. A gain equal to
            this threshold does not reset patience, even when the threshold is
            zero.
        start_step: Nonnegative warm-up boundary in the caller's step units.
            Stale observations at or before this step do not increment the
            counter; sufficient improvements still update the reference.
        objective: Direction selected at construction: `"min"` for lower values
            or `"max"` for higher values. Reassigning this field does not rebuild
            the comparison function.
        stale_steps: Mutable stale-evaluation counter, initially zero unless
            supplied to the constructor. It is not validated or reset by
            initialization; a sufficient improvement resets it to zero.
        reference_reward: Reference observation for measuring improvement,
            despite the reward-specific name. Initialized to positive infinity
            for minimization or negative infinity for maximization, then
            replaced by each sufficiently improved finite observation.
        _is_better: Implementation detail: comparison callable selected during
            initialization. It reads the current `reference_reward` and
            `min_delta` when evaluating an observation.

    """

    patience: int
    min_delta: float
    start_step: int
    objective: ObjectiveType

    stale_steps: int = 0

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate settings and initialize the reference and comparison function.

        Called automatically by the dataclass constructor.

        - Set the reference to positive infinity for `"min"`, or negative
          infinity for `"max"`.
        - Select the comparison direction from `objective`.
        - Leave `stale_steps` as supplied; this is not a full tracker reset.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If `patience` is nonpositive, `start_step` is negative,
                `min_delta` is nonfinite or negative, or `objective` is neither
                `"min"` nor `"max"`.
        """
        if self.patience <= 0:
            raise ValueError("patience must be positive")
        if self.start_step < 0:
            raise ValueError("start_step must be nonnegative")
        if not math.isfinite(self.min_delta) or self.min_delta < 0:
            raise ValueError("min_delta must be finite and nonnegative")
        if self.objective not in ("min", "max"):
            raise ValueError(
                f"objective should be 'min' or 'max' but got {self.objective}"
            )

        # First initialization.
        self.reference_reward = np.inf if self.objective == "min" else -np.inf

        if self.objective == "min":
            self._is_better = lambda current: current < (
                self.reference_reward - self.min_delta
            )
        else:
            self._is_better = lambda current: current > (
                self.reference_reward + self.min_delta
            )

    def update(self, value: float, step: int) -> bool:
        """Record one evaluation and report whether patience is exhausted.

        Apply the class's improvement and warm-up rules to mutate
        `reference_reward` and `stale_steps`. Reject nonfinite values before
        changing either field.

        Args:
            value: Finite observation to minimize or maximize. Compare against
                the stored reference using the strict `min_delta` threshold.
            step: Progress coordinate used only for comparison with `start_step`.
                Training passes the optimizer step. No monotonicity or
                nonnegativity check is performed; repeated calls at the same
                eligible step each count as an evaluation.

        Returns:
            stop_requested: Whether the current `stale_steps` is at least
                `patience`. This signal is not latched: a later sufficient
                improvement resets the counter and returns `False`.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If `value` is NaN or either infinity.

        Examples:
            Warm up through step 10, then stop after two stale evaluations. A gain
            exactly equal to `min_delta` does not count as an improvement. The
            reference starts at 10, stays unchanged at 12, then advances to 13.
            Observations of 14 and 15 exhaust patience against that reference.

            >>> tracker = EarlyStopping(2, 2.0, 10, objective="max")
            >>> tracker.update(10.0, step=0)
            False
            >>> tracker.update(12.0, step=10)
            False
            >>> tracker.update(13.0, step=11)
            False
            >>> tracker.update(14.0, step=20)
            False
            >>> tracker.update(15.0, step=30)
            True
        """
        if not math.isfinite(value):
            raise ValueError("Value tracked must be finite")

        if self._is_better(value):
            self.reference_reward = value
            self.stale_steps = 0
        else:
            if step > self.start_step:
                self.stale_steps += 1

        return self.stale_steps >= self.patience

items.title: evaluation
items.text:
Measure policy performance and retain evaluated checkpoints.

Two different measurements

  • compute_validation_loss averages batch losses weighted by example count.
  • evaluate_policy runs Push-T rollouts and averages each episode's maximum reward, not its reward sum.

Both temporarily use evaluation mode and restore the model's prior top-level training flag. Randomness is explicit: validation receives a generator, while rollouts derive separate indexed environment and policy streams.

save_checkpoint_and_retain keeps the best K evaluated checkpoints plus the latest. Video paths and retained checkpoint records refer to experiment-owned files; callers manage their longer-term lifecycle.

def resize_frame(frame: np.ndarray, size: tuple[int, int]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Resize an image array using PIL bilinear interpolation.

    Args:
        frame: Array accepted by `PIL.Image.fromarray`, normally an RGB render frame.
            This helper does not validate a particular color layout or dtype.
        size: Destination `(width, height)` passed directly to PIL.

    Returns:
        resized: NumPy representation of the resized image. Shape and dtype follow
            the PIL image mode; callers should not assume the returned array is writable.

    PIL conversion and size errors propagate. The input array is not modified.
    """
    image = Image.fromarray(frame)
    resized = image.resize(size, resample=Image.Resampling.BILINEAR)
    return np.asarray(resized)
