items.text:
train_step(model: BasePolicy, optimizer: Optimizer, state: Tensor, action_chunk: Tensor, *, generator: Generator) -> torch.Tensor

Compute loss, backpropagate, and take one optimizer step.

Set the model to training mode and clear gradients with set_to_none=True. Then call compute_loss, run backward, and update parameters. The caller must place the model and tensors on compatible devices. Mode, gradients, parameters, and consumed randomness are not restored on exit or failure.

Parameters:

  • model (BasePolicy) –

    Policy to train; expected to return a differentiable scalar loss.

  • optimizer (Optimizer) –

    Optimizer owning the policy parameters to update.

  • state (Tensor) –

    State batch already placed on the model device.

  • action_chunk (Tensor) –

    Target action windows in training coordinates on that device.

  • generator (Generator) –

    Caller-owned loss/dropout generator on the sampling device.

Returns:

  • loss ( Tensor ) –

    Detached loss tensor from before the parameter update, retaining its device. Detaching does not copy its storage.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/train.py 
def train_step(
    model: BasePolicy,
    optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
    state: torch.Tensor,
    action_chunk: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    generator: torch.Generator,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute loss, backpropagate, and take one optimizer step.

    Set the model to training mode and clear gradients with `set_to_none=True`.
    Then call `compute_loss`, run backward, and update parameters. The caller must
    place the model and tensors on compatible devices. Mode, gradients, parameters,
    and consumed randomness are not restored on exit or failure.

    Args:
        model: Policy to train; expected to return a differentiable scalar loss.
        optimizer: Optimizer owning the policy parameters to update.
        state: State batch already placed on the model device.
        action_chunk: Target action windows in training coordinates on that device.
        generator: Caller-owned loss/dropout generator on the sampling device.

    Returns:
        loss: Detached loss tensor from before the parameter update, retaining its
            device. Detaching does not copy its storage.
    """
    model.train()
    optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)

    loss = model.compute_loss(
        state=state,
        action_chunk=action_chunk,
        generator=generator,
    )

    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    return loss.detach()

items.title: run_training
items.text:
run_training(config: TrainConfig) -> None

Execute one fresh training run and write its experiment outputs.

Data and initialization

  • Use an available Torch accelerator, otherwise CPU. Download/load Push-T data and split whole episodes approximately 80/20 using the data-split stream.
  • For a fresh policy, fit normalization only on training episodes and initialize weights with the model-init stream. When loading a checkpoint, reuse its architecture and normalization; optionally override dropout.
  • Build window loaders using the actual model horizon. Start a new AdamW optimizer and step counter even when weights came from a checkpoint.

Reporting and selection

  • Report training-window means, validation loss, and selection rollouts at their configured intervals and the last scheduled training step.
  • Reuse training loss/loader generators across batches and epochs. Restart the validation-loss generator for every complete validation pass. Selection rollouts recreate indexed episode streams; final rollouts use separate streams.
  • Save after each selection evaluation, retaining best K plus latest. Optional plateau stopping counts eligible selection evaluations, with warm-up converted from epochs to optimizer steps.
  • On scheduled completion or plateau, reload the best currently tracked record by (score, step) and run final evaluation. With latest-only retention this normally selects the latest, not the best checkpoint from the full history. Failed-cleanup records remain tracked and can refer to missing local files; loading such a selected record propagates the failure.
  • Flush any remaining training-metric window after leaving the loops. Plateau stopping does not force an additional off-schedule validation pass.

Output ownership

Create a new exp/seed_<seed>_<timestamp>[_suffix] directory relative to the working directory. Own the W&B and progress contexts; reject offline W&B runs. Disable W&B explicitly for local-only training. CSV settings do not disable checkpoint creation or the experiment directory. Final-evaluation videos remain local; the final metric call does not submit their paths to W&B.

Persistent checkpoints stay under the experiment directory. When disabled, use temporary checkpoints for selection/final evaluation and remove them only on successful context exit. Failures propagate, close registered contexts, and may leave partial experiment outputs or temporary checkpoints for inspection. There is no transactional rollback or resumable optimizer/RNG-state snapshot.

Parameters:

  • config (TrainConfig) –

    Validated training settings. Loaded architecture overrides fresh-model options; current training, logging, and evaluation settings still apply.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    No complete training batches remain, W&B is offline, or a delegated configuration/data/policy validation fails.

  • FileExistsError –

    The generated experiment directory or a required fresh output destination already exists.

Dataset, device, filesystem, W&B, and encoding errors propagate. The function returns no trained model; retained checkpoints and reports are its outputs.

Source code in hw1/src/hw1_imitation/train.py 
def run_training(config: TrainConfig) -> None:
    """Execute one fresh training run and write its experiment outputs.

    **Data and initialization**

    - Use an available Torch accelerator, otherwise CPU. Download/load Push-T data
      and split whole episodes approximately 80/20 using the data-split stream.
    - For a fresh policy, fit normalization only on training episodes and initialize
      weights with the model-init stream. When loading a checkpoint, reuse its
      architecture and normalization; optionally override dropout.
    - Build window loaders using the actual model horizon. Start a new AdamW
      optimizer and step counter even when weights came from a checkpoint.

    **Reporting and selection**

    - Report training-window means, validation loss, and selection rollouts at their
      configured intervals and the last scheduled training step.
    - Reuse training loss/loader generators across batches and epochs. Restart the
      validation-loss generator for every complete validation pass. Selection
      rollouts recreate indexed episode streams; final rollouts use separate streams.
    - Save after each selection evaluation, retaining best K plus latest. Optional
      plateau stopping counts eligible selection evaluations, with warm-up converted
      from epochs to optimizer steps.
    - On scheduled completion or plateau, reload the best currently tracked record
      by `(score, step)` and run final evaluation. With latest-only retention this
      normally selects the latest, not the best checkpoint from the full history.
      Failed-cleanup records remain tracked and can refer to missing local files;
      loading such a selected record propagates the failure.
    - Flush any remaining training-metric window after leaving the loops. Plateau
      stopping does not force an additional off-schedule validation pass.

    **Output ownership**

    Create a new `exp/seed_<seed>_<timestamp>[_suffix]` directory relative to the
    working directory. Own the W&B and progress contexts; reject offline W&B runs.
    Disable W&B explicitly for local-only training. CSV settings do not disable
    checkpoint creation or the experiment directory. Final-evaluation videos
    remain local; the final metric call does not submit their paths to W&B.

    Persistent checkpoints stay under the experiment directory. When disabled,
    use temporary checkpoints for selection/final evaluation and remove them only
    on successful context exit. Failures propagate, close registered contexts, and
    may leave partial experiment outputs or temporary checkpoints for inspection.
    There is no transactional rollback or resumable optimizer/RNG-state snapshot.

    Args:
        config: Validated training settings. Loaded architecture overrides fresh-model
            options; current training, logging, and evaluation settings still apply.

    Raises:
        ValueError: No complete training batches remain, W&B is offline, or a
            delegated configuration/data/policy validation fails.
        FileExistsError: The generated experiment directory or a required fresh
            output destination already exists.

    Dataset, device, filesystem, W&B, and encoding errors propagate. The function
    returns no trained model; retained checkpoints and reports are its outputs.
    """
    streams = RandomStreamFactory(root_seed=config.seed)

    device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator()
    if device is None or not torch.accelerator.is_available():
        device = torch.device("cpu")

    zarr_path = download_pusht(config.data_dir)
    episodes_dataset = load_episodes_dataset(zarr_path=zarr_path)

    # We are not splitting out a test because policy performance is
    # evaluated through environment rollouts using separately controlled
    # evaluation randomness.
    train_episodes_subset, validation_episodes_subset = random_split(
        dataset=episodes_dataset,
        lengths=[0.8, 0.2],
        generator=streams.torch(
            StreamId.DATA_SPLIT,
            variation=config.data_split_variation,
        ),
    )

    if config.init_from is None:
        normalizer = Normalizer.from_episodes_data(episodes=train_episodes_subset)

        model = build_policy(
            PolicyConfig(
                policy_type=config.policy_type,
                state_dim=normalizer.state_dim,
                action_dim=normalizer.action_dim,
                chunk_size=config.chunk_size,
                hidden_dims=config.hidden_dims,
            ),
            cpu_generator=streams.torch(
                StreamId.MODEL_INIT,
                variation=config.model_init_variation,
                device="cpu",
            ),
            target_device=device,
        )

    else:
        model, normalizer, _ = load_policy(
            path=config.init_from,
            device=device,
        )

    if config.dropout_p is not None:
        override_dropout_p(model, config.dropout_p)
    device = next(model.parameters()).device

    # Create fresh for each training run; advance across its batches and epochs.
    # Streams with matching identities on the same backend reproduce the starting RNG state.
    train_loss_generator = streams.torch(
        StreamId.TRAIN_LOSS,
        variation=config.train_loss_variation,
        device=device,
    )

    train_loader, validation_loader = build_loaders(
        config=config,
        train_episodes=train_episodes_subset,
        validation_episodes=validation_episodes_subset,
        normalizer=normalizer,
        chunk_size=model.chunk_size,
        train_generator=streams.torch(
            StreamId.TRAIN_LOADER,
            variation=config.train_loader_variation,
        ),
        validation_generator=streams.torch(
            StreamId.VALIDATION_LOADER,
            variation=config.validation_loader_variation,
        ),
    )

    if len(train_loader) == 0:
        raise ValueError("No training batches; reduce batch_size or check the dataset.")

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        params=model.parameters(),
        lr=config.lr,
        weight_decay=config.weight_decay,
    )
    global_step = 0

    # Setup logging
    exp_name = f"seed_{config.seed}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}"
    if config.exp_name is not None:
        exp_name += f"_{config.exp_name}"

    # The training driver owns the directory and all output lifetimes.
    log_dir = Path(LOG_ROOT) / exp_name
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)

    total_steps = config.num_epochs * len(train_loader)
    stopper = (
        EarlyStopping(
            patience=config.early_stopping_patience,
            min_delta=config.early_stopping_min_delta,
            start_step=config.early_stopping_min_epochs * len(train_loader),
            objective="max",
        )
        if config.early_stopping_patience is not None
        else None
    )
    stop_requested = False
    stop_reason = "max_epochs"
    loss_sum = 0.0
    window_examples_count = 0

    display_metrics = {
        "epoch": f"1/{config.num_epochs}",
        "loss": "—",
        "val": "—",
        "eval": "—",
    }

    wandb_run_config = config_to_dict(config)
    wandb_run_config["model_config"] = asdict(model.config)
    wandb_run_config["training_config"] = {"dropout": get_dropout_config(model)}

    with ExitStack() as stack:
        # Checkpoint Directory management.
        # Auto clears temp dirs on successful completion only.
        checkpoint_dir = (
            log_dir / "checkpoints"
            if config.save_checkpoints
            else stack.enter_context(temp_checkpoint_dir(exp_name=exp_name))
        )

        run = (
            stack.enter_context(
                wandb.init(
                    project=config.wandb_project,
                    config=wandb_run_config,
                    name=exp_name,
                    dir=str(log_dir),
                )
            )
            if config.log_wandb
            else None
        )

        if run is not None and run.offline:
            raise ValueError(
                "Offline W&B is not supported by this training driver. "
                "Use --log-wandb False for local-only runs."
            )

        logger = ExperimentLogger(log_dir, run=run, log_csv=config.log_csv)
        checkpoints: dict[int, CheckpointRecord] = {}
        pending_cleanup: set[int] = set()

        if config.show_summary:
            model_device = next(model.parameters()).device
            device_label = str(model_device)
            if model_device.type == "cuda":
                device_label += f" · {torch.cuda.get_device_name(model_device)}"
            Console(stderr=True).print(
                build_training_summary(
                    config=config,
                    model=model,
                    run_name=exp_name,
                    device=device_label,
                    output_dir=log_dir,
                    dataset_path=zarr_path,
                    train_episodes=len(train_episodes_subset),
                    validation_episodes=len(validation_episodes_subset),
                    train_samples=len(
                        cast(Sequence, train_loader.dataset)
                    ),  # can be safely cast here since dataset does have len.
                    validation_samples=len(
                        cast(Sequence, validation_loader.dataset)
                    ),  # can be safely cast here since dataset does have len.
                    steps_per_epoch=len(train_loader),
                )
            )

        progress = stack.enter_context(
            tqdm(
                total=total_steps,
                desc="Train",
                unit="step",
                position=0,
                leave=True,
                dynamic_ncols=True,
                mininterval=0.5,
                miniters=1,
                disable=None,
                postfix=display_metrics,
            )
        )

        epoch = 0
        for epoch in range(config.num_epochs):
            display_metrics["epoch"] = f"{epoch + 1}/{config.num_epochs}"
            progress.set_postfix(display_metrics, refresh=False)
            for state, action_chunk in train_loader:
                loss = train_step(
                    model=model,
                    optimizer=optimizer,
                    state=state.to(device),
                    action_chunk=action_chunk.to(device),
                    generator=train_loss_generator,
                )
                global_step += 1

                # compute_loss() returns a batch mean. Weight it by the
                # number of examples before combining it with other batches.

                batch_examples = state.shape[0]
                loss_sum += loss.item() * batch_examples
                window_examples_count += batch_examples

                training_complete = global_step == total_steps
                eval_due = global_step % config.eval_interval == 0 or training_complete
                log_due = global_step % config.log_interval == 0 or training_complete
                validation_due = (
                    global_step % config.validation_interval == 0 or training_complete
                )

                if log_due:
                    mean_loss = loss_sum / window_examples_count

                    logger.log_train(
                        global_step=global_step,
                        epoch=epoch,
                        loss_window_mean=mean_loss,
                        window_examples_count=window_examples_count,
                    )

                    display_metrics["loss"] = f"{mean_loss:.4g}"
                    progress.set_postfix(display_metrics, refresh=False)

                    loss_sum = 0.0
                    window_examples_count = 0

                # Advance after the optimizer step; tqdm throttles redraws.
                progress.update(1)

                if validation_due:
                    # Restart validation RNG for each complete pass so checkpoints use
                    # matching draws, assuming unchanged batch order and sampling shapes.
                    validation_result = compute_validation_loss(
                        model=model,
                        loader=validation_loader,
                        device=device,
                        generator=streams.torch(
                            StreamId.VALIDATION_LOSS,
                            variation=config.validation_loss_variation,
                            device=device,
                        ),
                    )
                    logger.log_validation(
                        global_step=global_step,
                        loss_mean=validation_result.loss_mean,
                        examples_count=validation_result.examples_count,
                    )

                    display_metrics["val"] = f"{validation_result.loss_mean:.4g}"
                    progress.set_postfix(display_metrics, refresh=False)

                if eval_due:
                    progress.set_description_str("Evaluating")
                    video_dir = None
                    if config.num_video_episodes > 0:
                        video_dir = log_dir / "videos" / f"step_{global_step:08d}"
                        video_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)

                    result = evaluate_policy(
                        model=model,
                        normalizer=normalizer,
                        device=device,
                        chunk_size=model.chunk_size,
                        video_size=config.video_size,
                        num_video_episodes=config.num_video_episodes,
                        num_eval_episodes=config.eval_episodes,
                        flow_num_steps=config.flow_num_steps,
                        streams=streams,
                        env_stream=StreamId.EVAL_ENV,
                        policy_stream=StreamId.EVAL_POLICY,
                        env_variation=config.eval_env_variation,
                        policy_variation=config.eval_policy_variation,
                        video_dir=video_dir,
                        show_progress=not progress.disable,
                        progress_position=1,
                    )

                    logger.log_eval(
                        global_step=global_step,
                        mean_reward=result.mean_reward,
                        num_episodes=result.num_episodes,
                        video_paths=result.video_paths,
                    )

                    display_metrics["eval"] = f"{result.mean_reward:.3f}@{global_step}"
                    progress.set_postfix(display_metrics, refresh=False)

                    progress.set_description_str("Saving")

                    pending_cleanup = save_checkpoint_and_retain(
                        model=model,
                        step=global_step,
                        checkpoint_dir=checkpoint_dir,
                        run=run,
                        mean_reward=result.mean_reward,
                        top_k=config.checkpoint_top_k,
                        checkpoints=checkpoints,
                        normalizer=normalizer,
                        flow_num_steps=config.flow_num_steps,
                    )

                    if stopper is not None and not training_complete:
                        stop_requested = stopper.update(
                            step=global_step,
                            value=result.mean_reward,
                        )
                        if stop_requested:
                            stop_reason = "plateau"
                    progress.set_description_str("Train")

                final_eval_due = training_complete or stop_requested

                if final_eval_due:
                    progress.set_description_str("Running Final Evaluation")

                    # Retrieve best model / weights.
                    # NOTE: we tie break to last step; [nit] double descent.
                    best_step = max(
                        checkpoints, key=lambda step: (checkpoints[step].score, step)
                    )
                    best_model_record = checkpoints[best_step]
                    best_model, best_normalizer, inference = load_policy(
                        path=best_model_record.path, device=device
                    )

                    video_dir = None
                    if config.num_video_episodes > 0:
                        # TODO: confirm that the best_step here is in the same scale as global_step; not epochs.
                        video_dir = log_dir / "videos" / f"best_step_{best_step:08d}"
                        video_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)

                    # call final evaluation using evaluate_policy()
                    final_eval_result = evaluate_policy(
                        model=best_model,
                        normalizer=best_normalizer,
                        device=device,
                        chunk_size=best_model.chunk_size,
                        video_size=config.video_size,
                        num_video_episodes=config.num_video_episodes,
                        num_eval_episodes=config.final_eval_episodes,
                        flow_num_steps=inference["flow_num_steps"],
                        streams=streams,
                        env_stream=StreamId.FINAL_EVAL_ENV,
                        policy_stream=StreamId.FINAL_EVAL_POLICY,
                        env_variation=config.final_eval_env_variation,
                        policy_variation=config.final_eval_policy_variation,
                        video_dir=video_dir,
                        show_progress=not progress.disable,
                        progress_position=1,
                    )

                    logger.log_final_evaluation(
                        global_step=global_step,
                        mean_reward=final_eval_result.mean_reward,
                        num_episodes=final_eval_result.num_episodes,
                        checkpoint_step=best_step,
                        selection_mean_reward=best_model_record.score,
                        stop_reason=stop_reason,
                    )

                if stop_requested:
                    break
            if stop_requested:
                break

        if window_examples_count:
            logger.log_train(
                global_step=global_step,
                epoch=epoch,
                loss_window_mean=loss_sum / window_examples_count,
                window_examples_count=window_examples_count,
            )
        progress.set_description_str("Stopped (plateau)" if stop_requested else "Done")

        logging.info("Training ended at step %s: %s", global_step, stop_reason)
        if run is not None:
            run.summary["stop_reason"] = stop_reason

        if pending_cleanup:
            logging.warning(
                "Training finished with checkpoint cleanup pending for steps %s. "
                "Extra local files or W&B artifacts may remain.",
                sorted(pending_cleanup),
            )

def main() -> None:

items.title: Preview and build
items.text:
From the repository root:

Start a local preview
uv sync --locked
uv run --no-sync zensical serve
Build the static site
uv run --no-sync zensical build --strict

The site is written to site/. Documentation CI runs the strict build and whole-source documentation checks on every PR, on pushes to main, and on published releases. A separate trusted workflow publishes successful artifacts. Documentation dependencies are isolated from each training project's environment.

items.title: Add a page
items.text:
Add a Markdown file under docs/. Navigation discovers new pages automatically. Change the nearest .nav.yml only to control labels or order; keep its glob: "*" entry so unlisted pages still appear.

Use relative Markdown links such as [Test runs](../hw1/test-runs.md). Keep operational guides in docs/hw1/ and API pages in docs/reference/.

items.title: Write code examples
items.text:
Label fenced blocks with their language for syntax highlighting. Code blocks have a copy button. Add a filename with title, optional line numbers with linenums, and emphasized lines with hl_lines:

```python title="example.py" linenums="1" hl_lines="2"
from pathlib import Path
output = Path("exp")
print(output)
```
example.py
from pathlib import Path
output = Path("exp")
print(output)

items.title: Generate API documentation
items.text:
The native api-autonav integration discovers production modules beneath hw1/src/hw1_imitation and creates the Generated API section under /api/. Adding a class in that package requires no Markdown page or navigation entry. Discovery includes undocumented objects; generated does not mean reviewed. All production modules, classes, own members, and standalone functions under hw1/src are covered by the documentation gate. Tests under hw1/tests are outside this scope. Imported/re-exported and inherited objects are not counted as newly authored APIs.

Write Google-style docstrings beside the code. Use Attributes for class and stored instance fields, Args for parameters, and Returns or Yields for outputs. Document exception behavior in Raises. Keep meanings in Python source; shared templates derive signatures, types, and values from metadata.

Ordinary # comments appear in source disclosure but are not field descriptions. For an unannotated property return, use a named Google entry such as count (int): Number of entries. Do not change executable annotations merely for documentation. Inspection is disabled, so builds do not import training code.

Class coverage includes explicitly defined methods, properties, constructors, dunders, and private helpers; inherited members and synthesized constructors are not repeated. Private helpers are marked as implementation details.

Generated pages are canonical for Python-object links. Existing comparison pages retain their URLs and anchors but set skip_local_inventory: true, so their duplicate renderings do not register symbolic targets. Link from authored guides with [Normalizer][hw1_imitation.data.Normalizer]. Distinct pages can still appear separately in search during this comparison phase.

items.title: Validate production documentation
items.text:
After building, run the same gate used by CI:

Check production API documentation
uv tool install ruff==0.14.10
uv run --no-sync python scripts/check_docs.py --all --report docs-coverage.json

The default without --all is also whole-source enforcement. CI explicitly passes --all through scripts/build_docs.py before preparing an artifact. Ruff checks every production Python file; no training environment is installed. For a focused authoring check, use --pilot qualified.Class. This opt-in mode is not the CI gate. Its optional --baseline PATH compares that class's module against pre-edit source with docstrings removed.

The gate rejects missing or empty module/class/member/field/parameter/output documentation, stale fields and parameters, missing or empty structured raises, and missing/duplicate native API anchors or inventory entries. It reconciles AST and native class/function inventories, including private definitions. Explicit named raises outside try blocks require descriptions; caught, rethrown, dynamic, and dependency exceptions still need semantic review.

Function-local helpers are checked in source and reported as exceptions to native discovery: they have no independently generated API object or link. Function-local classes and arbitrary runtime-created attributes need explicit review. Structural checks cannot establish behavioral accuracy, validate every possible runtime object, or replace desktop/mobile rendered review.

items.title: Maintain the theme
items.text:
Navigation, search, code controls, and the light/dark toggle are native Zensical features. docs/stylesheets/theme.css customizes the palette, system font stacks, spacing, and borders. The shared mkdocstrings templates in docs-overrides/python/material/ combine structured Python attribute docstrings with source annotations and defaults when options.extra.documented_fields is enabled. Generated modules enable this strategy globally; the preserved comparison page opts in locally. A small function wrapper omits synthesized methods without source lines and labels private methods. Parameter, return, and exception sections use native lists to remain readable on mobile. Other rendering remains native. docs-theme/main.html adds a build/channel announcement to published pages using the native announcement block. There is no custom JavaScript.

Check both color modes and narrow screens when changing that stylesheet.

items.title: Publish documentation
items.text:
The public site uses GitHub Pages at https://00arun00.github.io/cs285_deep_rl_berkley/.

Path Source Lifecycle /latest/ Latest successful build of the current main commit Updated after merges /v1.0.0/ Published release tag v1.0.0 Immutable snapshot /stable/ Highest published semantic release Per-page redirects preserve deep links /previews/pr-38/ Successful PR build (GitHub's merge snapshot) Removed on close/merge or expiry; manual rebuilds can restore it / Redirect to /latest/ Permanent entry point

The release workflow supports published, non-prerelease tags named vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Merely pushing a tag does not publish docs: publish its GitHub Release. The tagged commit must contain the documentation build workflow and its locked tooling. Older versions remain available in the version selector; PR previews are excluded from that selector. Each published page identifies its channel and actual build commit. PR build records also retain the PR head and base commit. Preview pages carry noindex, nofollow metadata.

items.title: One-time setup and the first deployment
items.text:
1. In repository Settings → Pages, set Source → GitHub Actions.
  2. Enable Actions for this repository if GitHub disabled them when it was forked.
  3. In Settings → Environments → github-pages, restrict deployment branches to main. The publishing workflow runs in the default-branch context even when handling a release or PR build. No personal access token is required, and default workflow token permissions may remain read-only.
  4. Merge the reviewed publishing workflow into main. The resulting main build publishes /latest/. Before that merge, the infrastructure PR can validate and upload its artifact but cannot trigger its own trusted publisher.
  5. Verify the Publish documentation run and the live site. Existing open PRs need a new successful Documentation build or a manual publisher dispatch.

The publishing workflow and scripts always come from main; it never checks out or executes PR or release source in its privileged job. The read-only build job uploads static output. The publisher validates the workflow/run, current PR head or release tag, metadata and archive paths before consuming it. A PR cannot choose its deployment directory. For PRs, GitHub's recorded revision of the locally called build workflow must match the artifact's merge SHA. Builds without that provenance must be rebuilt with the updated workflow. Pages publication is serialized with queued runs. Automatic builds for superseded PR heads are skipped. A late build can restore a closed PR preview; expiry cleanup handles this accepted race. All output is retained on the machine-managed gh-pages branch; avoid editing that branch manually.

items.title: Rebuild and publish a preview
items.text:
Automatic PR builds use GitHub's synthetic merge checkout: the PR changes combined with its target branch. Main builds use the current main commit; release builds use the tagged commit. Build success and publication are separate operations. Publication is asynchronous and does not need to finish before merging.

Every successful PR build processed by the publisher records a snapshot named RUN_ID-ATTEMPT, for example 123456789-1. Find this ID in the preview comment or the publisher's Validate artifact and assemble all published versions log. Unapproved fork builds also get records; their IDs appear in that log. Records live under .docs-state/snapshots/ on gh-pages, independently of expiring build artifacts and preview pages. A failed build does not produce a rebuildable record.

To rebuild that exact source, including after the PR closes or merges:

  1. Open Actions → Rebuild and publish preview → Run workflow.
  2. Choose branch main and enter the snapshot ID.
  3. Run the workflow. This explicitly approves publication of that snapshot, including content from an external fork.

The workflow checks out the recorded merge commit, installs its locked build requirements, and runs the documentation checks and build. It publishes to the same previews/pr-N/ URL and updates the PR comment. This is a fresh build of the recorded source, not a new merge against today's main. If the commit can no longer be retrieved or its dependencies no longer build, the operation fails without substituting another commit. Old builds without snapshot records are unsupported.

Historical source executes in a read-only job without publishing credentials. The publisher runs separately using trusted main scripts. The manual workflow has no 30-day rerun-window restriction; it still depends on source availability.

items.title: Fork approval and retries
items.text:
PRs from branches within this repository publish automatically, even when this repository itself is a fork. PRs from an external fork require publication approval regardless of their target branch. Approval applies to the exact PR snapshot: retries of that snapshot reuse approval, but a changed head or merge snapshot needs fresh approval. GitHub's approval to run a fork build is separate.

An ordinary Re-run all jobs retries the original build and does not grant fork-publication approval. GitHub limits native reruns to 30 days after the original run. Use Rebuild and publish preview for older recorded snapshots.

To approve or retry publication of an existing successful artifact without rebuilding, open Publish documentation → Run workflow on main, select publish, and enter its Documentation run ID. The latest attempt must have succeeded. This action also approves its exact fork snapshot and can restore a closed PR's preview. Artifacts expire after 14 days; use the recorded snapshot rebuild when the artifact is gone. An obsolete main build cannot replace current main documentation. To retry a failed manual rebuild's publisher, rerun its failed jobs; the publisher can reuse that workflow run's already-successful build artifact.

A failed build leaves the last published preview intact. A failed deployment does not advance the preview's publication timestamp. The publisher retains pending state so a later deployment can finish it. Failed PR-comment updates are retained for retry independently of the website deployment. A comment API failure emits a warning and does not prevent deployment or updates to other PR comments.

items.title: Remove and expire previews
items.text:
Closing or merging a PR queues automatic removal of its preview. Cleanup checks that the PR is still closed before proceeding. A later explicit rebuild can restore the preview; a late automatic publication can also restore it. Both then follow the same expiry rule.

A daily cleanup runs at 03:17 UTC. It removes previews whose last successful publication is more than 30 days old, whether their PRs are open or closed. Set the repository Actions variable DOCS_PREVIEW_RETENTION_DAYS to a positive integer to change the retention period. PR creation time is not used. Successful publication resets the clock; failed builds and deployments do not.

For an immediate expiry sweep, open Publish documentation → Run workflow on main, select cleanup, and leave the run ID empty. This uses exactly the daily cleanup logic. To retry immediate removal after a failed close/merge event, rerun that event's failed Publish documentation job; an expiry sweep intentionally does not remove a recent preview merely because its PR is closed.

Cleanup removes preview files and updates their comments. Main/release versions, snapshot records, and approvals are retained. Removal from the current site does not erase Git history. Existing previews without timestamps get one retention period from their first successful migration deployment. If a deployment's final bookkeeping fails, a subsequent deployment recovers its pending state before expiry is considered.

items.title: Publishing implementation
items.text: mike is pinned to the Zensical-compatible fork in the optional publishing dependency group. It manages the version inventory, aliases, redirects and git commits. scripts/build_docs.py supplies the URL prefix and announcement metadata, then runs the strict build and existing checker. scripts/publish_docs.py uses the pinned mike API to publish already-built files; it deliberately does not use mike deploy, which would execute a build in the privileged job. Durable snapshot, approval, pending-deployment and publication records live in .docs-state/ on gh-pages; these internal records are excluded from the Pages artifact. Updates to mike must revalidate that API. The publishing job alone receives branch-write, Pages, OIDC, artifact-read and PR-comment permissions.

items.title: Start here: Push-T imitation learning
items.text:
The implementation in hw1/ trains a policy to imitate recorded demonstrations of Push-T: moving a T-shaped block into a target pose with a controllable pusher. A policy maps the current observation to actions; this implementation uses numeric state observations rather than camera images.

These guides assume you know Python, PyTorch, and basic supervised learning. Use this page to run or inspect the Push-T implementation. For other projects and their status, return to the repository overview.

items.title: Get started
items.text:
1. Prepare your environment: follow the HW1 setup instructions. Use the hw1/ working directory for HW1 commands.
  2. Exercise the pipeline: follow Run a small local training test. It explains output controls and remaining side effects. This is real training; it can download data and install dependencies.
  3. Check a code change: use the tests and checks for lint, formatting, and pytest commands.
  4. Understand the architecture: follow the conceptual reading path below, then use the source map and Python reference for implementation details.

For an existing trained policy, start with checkpoint loading and further training. Further training starts a fresh optimizer and run; it does not resume an interrupted training trajectory.

items.title: What is supported
items.text:
Training learns from recorded state–action pairs. Both supported policies predict an action chunk: a sequence of actions from one observation. mse predicts the chunk directly; flow transforms sampled noise into a chunk using a learned velocity field.

Environment rollouts assess the learned behavior and select checkpoints. Validation loss measures demonstration fit; rollout scores measure behavior under the policy's own actions. Their definitions and interpretation belong in the evaluation guide.

items.title: Understand the system
items.text:
Read the first four pages in order for the path from demonstrations to results. Use the final two when you need reproducibility or saved-policy details.

Page Question it answers Push-T task and dataset What are the observations, actions, demonstrations, and supported policy families? Demonstrations to training batches How do episode splits, normalization, chunks, and padding create examples? Training lifecycle How do optimization, monitoring, checkpoint selection, and final evaluation fit together? Evaluation and results What do the metrics mean, and how should comparisons account for variability? Randomness and reproducibility Which identities and generator lifetimes control random draws? Checkpoint format and lifecycle What survives saving, loading, retention, and cleanup?

items.title: Read the implementation
items.text:
Implementation modules below are relative to hw1/src/hw1_imitation/; tests are in hw1/tests/.

Entry point or module Start here when you want to understand… train.py CLI configuration and the training lifecycle. data.py Demonstration episodes, normalization, and action-chunk datasets. model.py MSE and flow policies, their losses, and action sampling. evaluation.py Validation, environment rollouts, and checkpoint selection/retention. checkpoint.py Saving and reconstructing a policy and its normalizer. randomness.py, rng_modules.py Named random streams and layers that consume explicit generators. logging_utils.py, early_stopping.py Run outputs and stopping when rollout improvement stalls. modal_train.py The optional remote-training entry point.

For a first code reading, follow train.py → data.py → model.py → evaluation.py. Return to the supporting modules when you need their specific behavior.

items.title: Common tasks
items.text:
• Configure and compare experiments.
  • Run a hyperparameter sweep.
  • Inspect results and diagnose a run.
  • Save, load, and train further.
  • Add a random stream.
  • Change the checkpoint format.
  • Change or add a policy.

For failures or unexpected behavior, use Troubleshooting to choose a diagnostic path.

Individual commands and sweep trials use the same training pipeline. Use a direct command for a chosen configuration, or a W&B sweep to search across configurations defined in hw1/conf/sweeps/. See CLI syntax and sweep configuration for their input formats.

items.title: Set up the Push-T development environment
items.text: Prepare the environment in hw1/ before running the small local test or automated checks.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• A local checkout of this repository.
  • A terminal with uv available on its PATH; installation is described below.
  • Network access for initial Python and dependency installation. A later training run may also download the Push-T dataset.

HW1 declares Python 3.11 or newer; its .python-version selects 3.11, which CI also uses. A GPU is optional: the trainer uses an available PyTorch accelerator, falling back to CPU.

items.title: Install uv if needed
items.text:
On macOS or Linux, use the command from the official uv installation instructions:

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

This downloads and executes Astral's installer, which installs uv and may update your shell setup. Open a new terminal afterward and check uv --version. Skip installation if uv is already available.

items.title: Install the locked environment
items.text:
From the repository root:

cd hw1
uv --version
uv python install
uv sync --locked --dev
  • uv python install obtains the Python version selected by .python-version when needed.
  • uv sync --locked --dev creates or updates the project environment using uv.lock, including development dependencies. It fails if the lockfile needs updating.
  • These setup commands may download packages and write environment/cache files. They do not start training or download demonstrations.

Keep subsequent HW1 commands in hw1/. Use uv run so commands use this project's environment; --no-sync reuses the installed environment without synchronizing dependencies again.

items.title: Verify the setup
items.text:
Run from hw1/:

uv run --no-sync python --version
uv run --no-sync src/hw1_imitation/train.py --help
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_checkpoint.py::test_cli_preserves_config_defaults -v

Expected results:

  1. Python reports a version compatible with the project (normally 3.11 with the checked-in version file).
  2. Trainer help lists options such as --policy-type, --num-epochs, and logging controls, without starting training.
  3. The named CLI-defaults test passes. This checks argument parsing against the configuration defaults; it does not establish that a real training run succeeds.

For the complete lint and test sequence, continue to Tests and checks.

See training CLI syntax for explicit boolean values and tuple arguments. To search across configurations after setup, follow Run a hyperparameter sweep.

items.title: Know which tools you need
items.text:
Tool Role When you need it uv Python and dependency management. Setup and project commands. PyTorch and the runtime dependencies Policies, data handling, and Push-T evaluation. Installed by the sync command. Ruff Lint and formatting checks. Before submitting code changes; included in project dependencies. pytest Run the existing test suite. Development; installed with --dev. Hypothesis Generate examples for property-based tests. Development; installed with --dev and used by pytest. JupyterLab Interactive exploration. Optional; included in --dev. Start with uv run --no-sync jupyter lab from hw1/. Weights & Biases Experiment reporting and artifact uploads. Optional service; the small-run recipe disables it. Modal Remote execution. Optional service; local development and tests do not require a Modal account.

The W&B and Modal Python packages are installed as runtime dependencies even when their services are unused. Ordinary training enables W&B by default; use the small-run recipe for a local run without login or uploads.

items.title: Enable W&B reporting only when needed
items.text:
For a run that should upload metrics and artifacts, authenticate from hw1/:

uv run --no-sync wandb login

Follow the prompt for your W&B API key. This contacts the service and saves authentication for later runs. Skip login for the small local test, which supplies --log-wandb False.

items.title: Keep documentation tooling separate
items.text: The repository-root environment builds the site; it does not replace the hw1/ environment. Return to the root before following documentation authoring.

items.title: Common setup mistakes
items.text:
Symptom Check uv is not found Open a new terminal after installation and confirm uv --version works. Trainer script or tests/ cannot be found Confirm the working directory is hw1/, not the repository root. A module or test tool is missing Run uv sync --locked --dev in hw1/, then retry through uv run --no-sync. Locked synchronization fails Check that pyproject.toml and uv.lock belong to the same checkout. Resolve the dependency mismatch before retrying. W&B asks for credentials during a local test Use every flag in the small-run recipe, including --log-wandb False.

For persistent environment, device, or CI differences, see Troubleshooting.

items.title: Run a small local training test
items.text: Exercise training, validation, and policy evaluation without W&B uploads, metric CSVs, or recorded videos. This recipe applies to the Push-T imitation trainer in hw1; it runs real training, not a dry run.

items.title: Before you run
items.text:
1. Complete environment setup and its CLI-help check.
  2. Open a terminal in hw1/. Allow dataset download if the data is absent, or supply an existing dataset as described below.
  3. Keep the complete flag set: each output control disables a different side effect.

The expectations below were checked against the implementation; this recipe was not executed as part of writing this guide. No measured runtime or score is implied.

items.title: Run locally
items.text:
From hw1/, run:

hw1 · terminal
uv run src/hw1_imitation/train.py \
  --log-wandb False \
  --log-csv False \
  --save-checkpoints False \
  --num-video-episodes 0 \
  --num-epochs 1 \
  --eval-episodes 1 \
  --final-eval-episodes 1

No W&B login is needed. The trainer uses an available accelerator, or CPU if none is available. Runtime depends on the machine; one epoch still processes the training loader; its final incomplete batch is dropped.

items.title: Recognize successful completion
items.text:
With the recipe unchanged, the source defines this sequence:

  1. A Push-T · Training summary table shows the effective configuration, dataset, device, and output directory.
  2. Training runs for one epoch. Validation and selection rollouts run at their configured intervals and at the final training step.
  3. The best retained checkpoint is loaded for a separate one-episode final evaluation.
  4. The process returns successfully after cleanup. In an interactive terminal, the progress description ends at Done; non-interactive output may suppress progress bars.

A returned shell prompt alone is not proof of success: check that there is no traceback and that the process exits with status zero. In a POSIX shell, run echo $? immediately after the training command to inspect its status.

This recipe deliberately leaves no metric CSVs, videos, or persistent policy checkpoints. The experiment directory remains, while the temporary checkpoint directory is removed after successful completion. Final scores are not persisted with both CSV and W&B logging disabled.

items.title: Limit external side effects
items.text:
Flag Effect --log-wandb False Skip W&B initialization, metrics, video uploads, and checkpoint artifacts. --log-csv False Do not create or append training, validation, evaluation, or final-evaluation CSVs. --save-checkpoints False Write checkpoints into a unique temporary directory. Remove that directory on success; retain it on failure. --num-video-episodes 0 Disable video recording for selection and final evaluation.

--save-checkpoints False does not disable checkpoint creation or W&B uploads by itself. Pair it with --log-wandb False for this local test. Temporary checkpoints are needed to load the best retained policy for final evaluation.

items.title: Reduce the run size
items.text:
Flag Effect --num-epochs 1 Train for one epoch instead of the default 400. --eval-episodes 1 Use one episode per selection evaluation instead of 100. --final-eval-episodes 1 Evaluate the best retained checkpoint for one episode instead of 100.

Validation and selection evaluation remain enabled, including selection evaluation at the last training step. Final evaluation runs separately. These small episode budgets check that the pipeline runs; they are insufficient for a reliable policy-quality comparison.

items.title: What still gets written
items.text:
• Experiment directory: exp/<run-name>/ is still created under hw1, even with all four side-effect controls set.
  • Temporary checkpoints: files are written to the system temporary directory. Failed runs retain them for inspection, subject to operating-system cleanup.
  • Dataset: missing data may be downloaded and extracted under data/.
  • Python environment: uv run may install dependencies and update its environment/cache when needed.

To reuse an existing dataset, append --data-dir /path/to/data-root. That directory should contain pusht/pusht_cchi_v7_replay.zarr. An existing pusht.zip can also be extracted without downloading it again. These flags do not enforce network isolation.

Use the local command above to avoid Modal execution. WANDB_MODE=offline is not a substitute for --log-wandb False: the trainer rejects offline W&B runs.

items.title: Inspect available options
items.text:
uv run src/hw1_imitation/train.py --help

The command uses the same hw1 working directory. Help displays the current flags and defaults without starting training.

items.title: If the run fails
items.text:
Symptom Next check Import error or missing script Confirm the hw1/ working directory and repeat the setup verification. Dataset download or extraction error Check network access, disk space, and the dataset layout under --data-dir. W&B login prompt or offline-mode error Confirm --log-wandb False is present; WANDB_MODE=offline alone does not disable W&B. No training batches The configured batch size exceeds the available training examples; reduce --batch-size or inspect the dataset. Temporary checkpoints remain Inspect the exception; failures retain temporary checkpoints and cleanup errors can leave partial contents.

Keep the traceback when diagnosing a failure. Run the relevant automated checks to separate code regressions from data or environment issues.

For more symptom-specific checks, see Troubleshooting.

items.title: Run tests and checks
items.text: Use the existing checks to verify a code change before trying a real experiment. Start with environment setup; all commands below run from hw1/ unless stated otherwise.

items.title: Run the CI checks locally
items.text:
After installing the locked development environment:

uv run --no-sync ruff check src tests
uv run --no-sync ruff format --check tests
uv run --no-sync pytest -v -rs
Check Expected result Ruff lint Exit successfully with no lint violations in src or tests. Ruff formatting Report that test files are already formatted. --check does not rewrite files. pytest Collected tests pass; -rs explains any skips.

CI checks formatting for tests only. The lint command checks both source and tests. A missing test dependency is a setup problem: run uv sync --locked --dev before retrying.

items.title: Narrow a test run
items.text:
Run an entire test file:

uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_checkpoint.py -v

Run one existing test:

uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_checkpoint.py::test_cli_preserves_config_defaults -v

Select the flow variants in the checkpoint file:

uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_checkpoint.py -k flow -v

Use a focused selection while investigating a failure, then run the full CI sequence before handing off the change. Check the collected/selected count: a misspelled node or filter can leave the intended behavior untested.

items.title: Find the relevant test group
items.text:
Files below are under hw1/tests/.

Area Existing files Contracts checked Data test_data_boundaries.py Episode reconstruction, chunk boundaries, padding, indexing, and source-data isolation. Numerical behavior test_numerical_correctness.py Example-weighted validation loss, mean episode-maximum rollout scores, and flow integration against a known solution. Checkpoint loading and writing test_checkpoint.py, test_checkpoint_atomicity.py Policy round trips, fresh training from saved weights, invalid formats, and preserving files when serialization fails. Retention test_checkpoint_retention.py, test_checkpoint_retention_properties.py Best/latest selection, ties, and cleanup retries after failures. Randomness test_randomness.py, test_evaluation_streams.py Stable stream identities, isolation, replay, and separation of final evaluation. Dropout test_generator_dropout.py, test_rng_modules.py, test_dropout_integration.py Explicit-generator behavior, evaluation mode, layer configuration, and checkpoint restoration. CLI and sweep configuration test_sweep_config.py Explicit-value syntax, caller defaults, and both conf/sweeps/ YAMLs through W&B argument expansion into the shared CLI. Training outputs and control test_logging_controls.py, test_training_reporting.py, test_training_summary.py, test_evaluation_budgets.py, test_early_stopping.py Output switches, loss reporting, summary content, evaluation budgets, and plateau stopping.

Some cases use Hypothesis to explore generated inputs; others parameterize policy families or output settings. A test file can therefore collect many cases.

items.title: What passing tests establishes
items.text:
The suite uses synthetic demonstrations and mocked data access, physics environments, and W&B services for training integration checks. It also exercises real tensor operations, policy serialization, and local file handling.

Sweep checks use the installed W&B argument-expansion helper with representative parameter values and mock training. They do not register a sweep, run Bayesian search, or verify live W&B execution.

  • It does not require downloading the Push-T dataset or contacting W&B.
  • It writes temporary files and may write pytest, Python, and Hypothesis caches.
  • An accelerator-transfer test skips when no accelerator is available. That skip does not mean CPU coverage failed; a pass does not establish GPU training coverage.
  • Passing tests do not verify real environment rollouts, remote uploads, or a real-data training run. Use the small local training test for the next level of integration.

items.title: How CI relates to these commands
items.text:
The HW1 workflow runs the HW1 checks job on Ubuntu 24.04 for every pull request, regardless of target branch, and pushes to main.

It installs Python from hw1/.python-version, runs uv sync --locked --dev, and executes the three commands above from hw1/. Local success is useful evidence; CI also checks the Linux environment.

Documentation has a separate environment and workflow. For site changes, follow documentation authoring from the repository root rather than installing site tools into HW1.

items.title: Troubleshoot a Push-T run
items.text:
Start with the first failing operation, its full traceback, the exact command, and the run directory if one was created. The checks below distinguish configuration, environment, data, and code failures; they are diagnostic steps, not claims that a remedy has been tested on your machine.

Run HW1 commands from hw1/ after setup. Preserve logs and partially written artifacts until you understand the failure.

items.title: Find the relevant symptom
items.text: Symptom Start here Missing command, import, script, or locked dependency Environment and working directory Download/extraction error, missing Zarr key, invalid episodes Dataset and cache Invalid option, no batches, or video dimensions Configuration and sample counts Device error or out-of-memory failure Device and memory Checkpoint will not load Checkpoint compatibility Same seed produces surprising differences Randomness and repeatability Missing metrics, videos, or policy files Outputs and cleanup Local checks and CI disagree Local versus CI

items.title: Environment and working directory
items.text:
Symptom Check and next step Verify uv is not found Check shell PATH; open a new terminal after installation. Follow setup if needed. uv --version succeeds. Script or tests/ not found Confirm the working directory is hw1/, not the documentation root. The relative paths in tests and checks exist. Import error or missing pytest/Hypothesis Use the HW1 environment and its locked development dependencies. Follow setup's sync procedure. Trainer --help and the named CLI-defaults test in setup verification succeed. Locked synchronization fails Check that the manifest and lockfile are from the same checkout and that Python meets the project's requirements. Resolve the mismatch rather than bypassing the lock. Locked synchronization succeeds without an unintended dependency change.

HW1 selects Python 3.11 through .python-version; the root environment is for documentation. A successful site build does not establish that HW1 dependencies are installed.

items.title: Dataset and cache
items.text:
The expected store is <data-dir>/pusht/pusht_cchi_v7_replay.zarr. The loader consumes data/state, data/action, and meta/episode_ends; see artifact and field contracts.

Symptom Check and supported next step Verify Download fails Inspect the original network/filesystem error, available disk space, and write access. For a known-good existing dataset, use --data-dir to its root. The intended Zarr store can be opened and its required arrays read. BadZipFile or extraction failure Inspect the cached pusht.zip and extraction target. The downloader reuses an existing ZIP and does not repair partial downloads. A deliberately replaced or separately recovered artifact has the expected layout and readable arrays. Existing directory but missing arrays/keys The downloader returns immediately when the expected Zarr path exists; existence is not an integrity check. Preserve the partial cache and investigate the missing fields. All three required fields load, then episode validation succeeds. Unequal packed lengths or invalid episode ends Compare state/action row counts and exclusive offsets. Do not manufacture offsets to suppress the error. Ends are positive, strictly increasing, and finish at the total row count. Empty or malformed episodes/statistics Check data shape, contents, and representation against the data pipeline. Nonempty compatible episodes produce valid finite normalization statistics.

A failed download can leave an incomplete ZIP; a failed extraction can leave a misleadingly present Zarr directory. Repeating the same command may reuse that state. There is no automatic checksum verification or partial-cache repair.

If recovery requires another download or replacing files, first preserve the failed artifact and decide explicitly which cache to replace. A separate data root avoids overwriting evidence, but can cause a fresh download. No deletion or repair command is prescribed here.

items.title: Configuration and sample counts
items.text:
These messages originate in the implementation:

Message or symptom Next step Verify <name> must be positive Use positive epoch/batch/chunk/interval/episode counts and flow steps. Read current flags with trainer --help. Argument parsing accepts the corrected value. dropout_p must be in [0, 1) Use zero to disable dropout, or a probability below one. Effective summary reflects the intended dropout settings. checkpoint_top_k must be nonnegative Use K≥0; K=0 means latest-only retention. Configuration parses; interpret final selection accordingly. Video dimensions must be positive and even Supply positive even dimensions, or set --num-video-episodes 0 when videos are unnecessary. Configuration parses; later recording requires the encoding environment too. No training batches; reduce batch_size or check the dataset. Training drops its incomplete final batch. Reduce batch size or inspect available examples. At least one complete training batch exists. no valid chunks: reduce chunk_length or enable padding Check episode lengths against horizon; the trainer enables final-action padding by default. Per-episode windows exist without crossing boundaries. validation loader produced no examples Inspect split size and window availability, especially with tiny custom data. Validation contains examples; do not replace an undefined loss with zero.

A loaded checkpoint supplies its own chunk horizon, so changing --chunk-size does not resize it. See save/load settings.

items.title: Device and memory
items.text:
The trainer selects an available PyTorch accelerator, otherwise CPU. It has no --device CLI option and does not automatically retry on CPU after an accelerator operation fails.

  • Unavailable device while loading: the direct load_policy(..., device="cpu") API supports CPU loading. Confirm the checkpoint loads there before investigating accelerator support; this is not a trainer-device flag.
  • Generator/device mismatch: put sampling tensors and their Torch generator on compatible devices. Moving the model alone is insufficient.
  • Accelerator out of memory: reducing batch size is a diagnostic option for training tensors. Smaller fresh-model widths or horizons change the experiment; they do not reshape a loaded model.
  • Host memory pressure: data loading materializes packed arrays, normalization concatenates training episodes, and prepared datasets can allocate more arrays. Reducing batch size may not address this stage. Identify whether failure occurs during preparation or training before changing settings.

Verify with the smallest relevant API/test path first, then a deliberately chosen integration run. These checks do not establish accelerator training support or a universal memory requirement.

items.title: Checkpoint compatibility
items.text:
Symptom Check and next step Verify Unsupported checkpoint format; expected version 1 Confirm the file came from this policy writer. Legacy whole-model pickle and earlier experimental resume schemas are unsupported. A supported file loads through load_policy; do not bypass the format check. Missing component or strict weight-load error Check producing revision, architecture, and weight keys/shapes. Follow format-change guidance for an intentional migration. Reconstruction and raw-space predictions match the intended policy. Invalid normalization statistics/dimensions Check saved means/scales and architecture compatibility. Do not refit statistics merely to make an old policy load. Valid statistics match the model's state/action dimensions and original semantics. Configured dropout layer names do not match the model Check architecture changes or renamed modules. Saved dropout names must match reconstruction. A compatible checkpoint restores layer probabilities and evaluation mode. Checkpoint flow_num_steps must be a positive integer Inspect the producing format/configuration; this field is validated even for MSE. Supported payload contains a valid default and loads normally.

A checkpoint is not exact training resumption: optimizer moments, RNG position, and training position are absent. See save, load, and train further rather than interpreting new counters as lost resume state.

items.title: Randomness and repeatability
items.text:
For differing results, compare code, data, backend, configuration, root seed, stream variations, and sampling shapes before calling the run nondeterministic.

Symptom Check Verify Identical noise repeats every batch Is the generator recreated with the same identity inside the loop? Retain it to advance. Sequential draws advance; a deliberate recreation replays the start. Changing monitoring affects training Look for a shared/global RNG or changed draw routing. Existing isolation checks pass; see stream maintenance. Final score differs from selection Final evaluation has separate streams and possibly another budget. Compare selected step and budgets in the final row. CPU and accelerator results differ Backend, operation, and library behavior can affect replay despite matching integer seeds. Compare within a controlled backend before interpreting cross-device differences. Active dropout requires a caller-owned generator Pass the generator through the entire nested module path. Training-mode dropout works and evaluation mode disables its draws.

Use randomness contracts and repeat comparisons across seeds; one fixed seed does not measure robustness.

items.title: Outputs and cleanup
items.text:
Symptom Check and next step Verify CSV files absent Was --log-csv False supplied, or did failure precede logger creation? Inspect expected files using the results guide. W&B login prompt or offline error Use --log-wandb False for local-only work. Offline mode alone is unsupported. A chosen local run does not initialize W&B. Videos absent Check num_video_episodes, completed rollouts, and recording errors. CSV logging does not control recording. Look in the correct selection/final video directory. Checkpoint absent after success --save-checkpoints False uses temporary storage that is removed on success; retention can remove older persistent files. Compare flags and selected step with retention rules. Temporary checkpoints remain after failure They are intentionally retained when the training body raises; cleanup itself can also fail. Preserve them while diagnosing. Read the original exception and confirm which storage path remains. Extra files/artifacts or cleanup warnings Failed deletions remain tracked for retry during the process; retry state does not persist across runs. Inspect actual local/remote state before choosing manual cleanup.

--save-checkpoints False does not disable W&B uploads. Final CSV output can precede a later W&B reporting or cleanup failure. Use process status and traceback together with artifacts when deciding whether the run succeeded.

items.title: Local versus CI
items.text:
CI runs the documented HW1 checks on Linux with Python from hw1/.python-version and locked development dependencies.

  1. Compare the failing job and command: documentation and HW1 checks use different environments.
  2. Match the tested revision, dependency lock, working directory, and Python version locally.
  3. Run the failing existing test selection, then the complete check sequence.
  4. Read skip reasons: the accelerator-transfer test skips when hardware is unavailable; that does not establish GPU-training coverage.
  5. If the same code passes locally, preserve the CI traceback and investigate platform/device or environment differences rather than changing the assertion blindly.

A useful handoff includes the exact command, revision, Python/backend details, traceback, relevant flags, and expected versus observed files. Exclude credentials from logs you share.

items.title: CLI and sweep configuration
items.text:
Symptom Next check Expected result An old boolean flag is rejected Replace bare flags and --no-* forms with explicit values such as --log-wandb False. The shared CLI accepts the value. A tuple argument is rejected Quote a Python tuple literal, such as --hidden-dims "(256, 256, 256)". One tuple argument reaches the parser. Sweep YAML is not found Run from hw1/ and use conf/sweeps/mse.yaml or conf/sweeps/flow.yaml. W&B can read the chosen definition. A changed YAML seems ignored Register the edited definition and use its new sweep ID. New trials use the new registered settings.

For registration, trial execution, and results, follow Run a hyperparameter sweep.

items.title: Policy checkpoints and retention
items.text: A checkpoint reconstructs a policy for inference or initializes a new training run. It does not capture the entire running experiment. That boundary determines what can be reused and what must start fresh.

items.title: What version 1 stores
items.text:
Field Contents format_version The supported policy schema version, currently 1. model_config Policy type, state/action dimensions, chunk size, and hidden widths. model_state_dict Learned parameter tensors saved on CPU. training_config.dropout Per-layer dropout probabilities keyed by module name. normalizer State/action means and scales. inference_config.flow_num_steps Default integration-step count for flow sampling.

Not stored: optimizer moments, epoch/step position, generator states, data-split membership, loader position, or checkpoint-retention history. Earlier experimental resume schemas and legacy whole-model .pkl files are unsupported.

items.title: Loading reconstructs the model
items.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Read tensors onto CPU] --> B[Check version and required components]
    B --> C[Reconstruct architecture and normalization]
    C --> D[Strictly load weights]
    D --> E[Restore dropout settings]
    E --> F[Move model to requested device]
    F --> G[Return model in evaluation mode]

load_policy returns (model, normalizer, inference_config). It uses torch.load(..., weights_only=True) and does not consume default random streams while reconstructing weights. Normalization remains in CPU NumPy arrays; inference randomness is still the caller's responsibility.

Validation includes:

  • Supported outer format/version and required components as they are used.
  • Valid architecture and normalization dimensions.
  • Finite means, finite positive scales, and a positive integer flow-step default.
  • Exact weight keys/shapes through strict state-dict loading.
  • Matching dropout-layer names and valid probabilities.

This is not an exhaustive up-front schema validator. Malformed contents can raise KeyError, TypeError, or PyTorch errors as well as ValueError. An unavailable requested device raises; the loader does not fall back to CPU automatically.

items.title: Further training starts a new run
items.text:
Reused from checkpoint Taken from the new invocation Architecture and weights. Optimizer, learning rate, epoch budget, counters, root seed, and logging run. Normalizer. Demonstrations and their newly selected split. Per-layer dropout, unless explicitly overridden. Evaluation budgets and flow integration steps.

--policy-type, --hidden-dims, and --chunk-size affect fresh models only. With --init-from, loaders and rollouts use the loaded model's horizon. New data must have compatible dimensions and meaning; matching shapes alone cannot establish compatibility.

--dropout-p explicitly overrides all dropout layers, including when set to zero. If omitted, saved probabilities survive. The new training invocation uses its own --flow-num-steps, rather than inheriting the saved inference default.

Use the save, load, and further-training guide for commands. The checkpoint API describes detailed contracts.

items.title: Atomic replacement protects the destination
items.text:
save_policy validates the inference settings and dimensions, assembles the payload, then writes a sibling file such as policy.pt.tmp. Only after serialization succeeds does it replace policy.pt; cleanup removes the temporary path.

  • A serialization failure before replacement preserves an existing destination.
  • Errors propagate; cleanup itself can fail.
  • Writers targeting the same path share a temporary filename and must not run concurrently.
  • Keep model weights and statistics stable while saving: detached CPU parameter tensors are not necessarily copies.
  • Atomic replacement does not promise crash-durable storage.

Existing atomicity tests exercise preservation when serialization fails; see Tests and checks.

items.title: Keep the best K plus latest
items.text:
Every selection evaluation saves policy_step_<step>.pt. Default persistent storage is the run's checkpoints/ directory.

Rule Effect Higher rollout score ranks first. Selection uses mean_reward, not validation loss. Equal scores favor later steps. The more recent tied policy ranks higher. Keep the top K and latest. With default K=3, successful cleanup leaves at most four distinct checkpoints. K=0. Successful cleanup keeps only latest.

Illustrative K=1 example: step 10 scores 0.8, step 20 scores 0.6. Both remain: step 10 is best, step 20 is latest. If step 30 scores 0.8, it wins the tie and is also latest; successful cleanup removes steps 10 and 20.

Final evaluation chooses the highest-scoring retained record. With K=0 and successful cleanup, only latest is available, even if an earlier deleted checkpoint scored better.

items.title: Storage flags and failure handling
items.text:
--save-checkpoints False switches to temporary storage; it does not disable saving, retention, or W&B uploads. Temporary files are needed for final evaluation. Normal completion removes that directory; a raised training error leaves it for inspection, subject to operating-system cleanup.

With W&B enabled, saving proceeds locally, then uploads a model artifact and waits for completion before pruning. Uploads move latest, and move best when K is positive and the new step ranks first. Offline W&B is rejected.

Failure Result Local save or upload fails. Error propagates; a newly written local checkpoint may remain. No rollback is promised. Local deletion fails. Log the failure and keep the record for retry. Remote deletion fails after local deletion. Keep the record for retry, although its local file may already be gone. Cleanup still pending at shutdown. Warn that extra files or artifacts may remain; retry state does not survive the process.

Cleanup failures can leave more records than the normal retention limit. Because final selection uses retained records, failed cleanup can also affect which records remain candidates. Videos and W&B caches are outside checkpoint retention.

For the actual scheduling and final-selection point, return to the training lifecycle.

For serialization changes, follow Change the checkpoint format.

items.title: From demonstrations to training batches
items.text:
The data pipeline preserves episode boundaries and turns each observation into an action-chunk prediction problem. Fresh policies fit normalization on training data; checkpoint-initialized policies reuse saved statistics. Paths and array names are described in Push-T data.

flowchart TD
    A[Load whole episodes] --> B[Split episodes 80 / 20]
    B --> C[Training subset]
    B --> D[Validation subset]
    C --> E{Initialize from checkpoint?}
    E -->|No| F[Fit statistics on training timesteps]
    E -->|Yes| G[Load policy and saved statistics]
    F --> H[Build fresh policy]
    H --> I[Normalize both subsets]
    G --> I
    C --> I
    D --> I
    I --> J[Build episode-local windows using model horizon]
    J --> K[Training and validation loaders]

Both paths build windows using the actual model horizon. With --init-from, new demonstrations must match the loaded policy’s dimensions and coordinate meaning; see checkpoint semantics.

items.title: Load and split episodes
items.text:
The loader opens Zarr read-only and materializes the three required arrays in memory. For example, exclusive ends [3, 7] describe episodes covering rows [0:3] and [3:7].

Checks require:

  • Matching numbers of state and action rows.
  • A nonempty, one-dimensional sequence of positive, strictly increasing ends.
  • The final end to equal the total number of rows.
  • Nonempty episodes with two-dimensional float32 state/action arrays.

Zarr end offsets are cast to int64 before these boundary checks; the loader is not an exhaustive validation of the original stored dtypes. Episode views share backing storage and are marked read-only, so callers should not mutate writable aliases.

run_training uses an 80/20 random split of episodes, controlled by the data-split stream. Whole trajectories stay in one subset. The fraction is by episode count, not timesteps; unequal episode lengths can produce different sample proportions. There is no third demonstration test subset: final performance is measured in environment rollouts.

items.title: Fit and reuse normalization
items.text:
For a fresh policy, concatenate training-episode timesteps and compute a mean and population standard deviation for each state/action feature. Each scale is floored at 1e-6.

normalized feature = (raw feature - training mean) / training scale
raw action         = normalized action * action scale + action mean
